meta.title: gravyflow model zoo: literature catalogue (metrics, runtime, code, comparability)
meta.status: Read-only research output, work in progress. Every number is the paper's, located by table, figure or section; "read-from-figure" values carry reading error. Comparability grades and highlighted errors are the synthesiser's judgement. Every model's gravyflow reproduction is pending.
meta.starting_point: The literature review of the author's PhD thesis (Cardiff University), extended by citation and venue searches

effort_scale.S: model code and configuration on the existing data path (days)
effort_scale.M: one new library feature or substantial data work (about 1-2 weeks)
effort_scale.L: several new features, an external pipeline or dataset, or a new physics domain
effort_scale.-: nothing to do (shipped) or not assessable (unread)

badaracco2020.title: Machine learning for gravitational-wave detection: surrogate Wiener filtering for the prediction and optimized cancellation of Newtonian noise at Virgo
badaracco2020.reason: Not applied to GW strain (uses seismic correlations; Virgo is not NN-limited so C_NN is modelled, not measured); one hour of data; universality of c(N)=a(1-1/bN) is unexplained; no real cancellation test.

baltus2022light.title: A machine learning approach to the search for gravitational waves emitted by light objects (PhD thesis)
baltus2022light.reason: Thesis body not read. The ML content is a compilation of Baltus et al. 2021 (PRD 103, 102003; baltus2021), the CBMI 2021 paper (baltus2021b), Baltus et al. 2022 (PRD 106, 042002; baltus2022), plus a sub-solar-mass matched-filter search and a sky-localisation chapter whose papers are not in the catal

boudart2023.title: Detection of minute-long Gravitational Wave transients using Deep Learning methods (PhD thesis)
boudart2023.reason: Thesis body not read. Its ML chapters correspond to catalogue entries boudart2022 (ALBUS, arXiv 2201.08727) and boudart2022glitch (arXiv 2210.04588).

khan2021.title: AI and extreme scale computing to learn and infer the physics of higher order gravitational wave modes of quasi-circular, spinning, non-precessing binary black hole mergers
khan2021.reason: Trained and tested on noiseless NRHybSur3dq8 surrogate waveforms; no detector noise or detector data is used anywhere (PyCBC comparison uses a flat PSD only to set the likelihood). It is a waveform-manifold regression study. Flagged for the owner: keep only as a noise-free PE reference, not as a detector-data model.

mitra2023.title: Probing nuclear physics with supernova gravitational waves and machine learning
mitra2023.reason: No detector noise, no SNR/distance dependence, no detection stage; axisymmetric sims lack realistic prompt convection; one progenitor; classification of EOS labels not regression. Not an ML-on-detector-data model: the network is trained and tested on noise-free simulated waveforms, so is_ml_on_gw_de

puecher2024.title: A machine-learning classifier for the postmerger remnant of binary neutron stars
puecher2024.reason: Trained on NR simulation parameters, not on detector data; classifier outputs depend on NR physics and EoS coverage (authors state this is the dominant uncertainty).

whittaker2022.title: Using machine learning to parametrize postmerger signals from binary neutron stars
whittaker2022.reason: Not applied to detector data, noise, detection or parameter inference; the proof of principle is on a synthetic generator derived from the same 123 fits.

dropped_by_sweep.reason: Classifier acts on simulated population-level parameters (Pop III vs other BBH populations), not trained on or applied to detector strain data

conventions.note: FAR per month uses 30-day months (MLGWSC-1). A FAR is converted only when the paper states a rate per unit time, or a per-segment fraction over disjoint segments of stated length (the conversion is then exact and noted).

axes.eff@FAR: Detection efficiency (TPR) at a FAR that is a rate per unit time; far_hz and far_per_month given.
axes.reach@FAR: Sensitive distance or volume (or hrss50 for bursts) at a stated FAR; the search-grade comparison.
axes.eff@FAP: TPR at a per-window or per-sample false-alarm probability: not a rate; comparable only with the same window length, noise and SNR distribution.
axes.AUC: Area under ROC; quoted only where noise and SNR distribution are stated, otherwise noted as such.
axes.GS: Glitch classification on a Gravity Spy release: accuracy and macro-F1 with release, class count and split.
axes.overlap: Denoising/extraction: overlap or match with the injected waveform.
axes.range: Noise regression: BNS inspiral-range or VT gain on real data.
axes.PE: Parameter estimation: calibration (P-P / coverage), bias or JSD against a sampler, sampling efficiency.
axes.depth@pfa: Continuous waves: sensitivity depth at a false-alarm probability per frequency band.
axes.events: Real catalogue events recovered (supplementary; never a substitute for efficiency at FAR).
axes.other: A headline metric outside the shared axes.

grades.comparable: Same contract as a published reference (MLGWSC-1, LVK injection sets, Gravity Spy split with re-trained baselines, CW depth at pfa), so numbers can be set side by side.
grades.conditional: On a shared axis but with a stated difference (noise, population, detector count, dataset release, relative-only gain).
grades.not: No shared axis: per-window fractions, private toy sets, qualitative or unread.

v4_changes.added_from: docs/model-zoo/thesis/thesis-models.json (the owner's own thesis models, origin 'added', thesis true)
v4_changes.owner_reproductions_field: List on the reproduced model's entry: what, metrics (each with conditions and location), gravyflow_version, notes, source. The v3 fields of those entries are unchanged.
v4_changes.counts_method: Each count moved by the thesis models' contribution from its v3 value.

v5_changes.source: Every catalogued paper in the archive was read for latency, inference cost and training cost; a second, independent reader checked every number and every "none stated" against the paper. Records the check rejected are dropped; each kept record carries the check's verdict in `check`.
v5_changes.unread: Models whose paper is not in the archive carry `runtime_unread` (the reason) and an empty list; they are never counted as stating none.
v5_changes.counts_method: meta.counts.runtime.models_with[quantity][grade] counts models with at least one record of that quantity and grade; `any` counts models with at least one record of the quantity.

in-window.name: Window length
in-window.state: Have: any onsource length, fixed CBC buffer B(W)=2^ceil(log2 2W). Gap: windows of 10-300 s are unmeasured for memory and generation cost.

in-multirate.name: Multi-rate input
in-multirate.state: Have: one sample rate per dataset, one resampler. Gap: a window cut into segments at different rates (Schafer 2020, Nagarajan 2025).

in-stft.name: STFT spectrogram
in-stft.state: Have: gf.spectrogram / SPECTROGRAM_ONSOURCE (|STFT|^2 of whitened data, Hann frames). Gap: per-paper window, overlap, log scaling, band crop, image resize.

in-qtransform.name: Q-transform / Omega-scan images
in-qtransform.state: Gap: no Q-transform in gravyflow; Gravity Spy-style multi-duration (0.5/1/2/4 s) images, CQT, colour maps and resizing to backbone inputs.

in-wavelet.name: Wavelet transforms
in-wavelet.state: Gap: wavelet packet, CWT (Morlet), scattering transform, cWB-like WDF time-frequency maps.

in-freqdomain.name: Frequency-domain input
in-freqdomain.state: Gap: real/imaginary whitened rfft as model input (DINGO, CW nets); PSD-as-input channels.

in-mf-series.name: Matched-filter front end
in-mf-series.state: Have: MatchedFilter, MatchedFilterLayer (returns network-SNR logits), TemplateBank. Gap: per-template SNR time series and template-by-time SNR maps as model inputs, top-k template selection, learnable template layer (MFCNN).

in-pearson.name: Cross-detector correlation
in-pearson.state: Have: ROLLING_PEARSON_ONSOURCE (circular shift; lag convention not pinned). Gap: frequency-domain correlation features.

in-aux.name: Auxiliary witness channels
in-aux.state: Gap: gravyflow reads strain only; no auxiliary-channel acquisition (needs LocalFrames on a LIGO cluster, non-public channels).

in-pipeline-triggers.name: External pipeline triggers
in-pipeline-triggers.state: Gap: cWB, Omicron, PyCBC or BAYESTAR products as inputs (cWB summary statistics, reconstructed waveforms, skymaps).

in-pretrained.name: Pretrained backbones
in-pretrained.state: Gap: ImageNet / audio pretrained weights (keras.applications under the JAX backend, Whisper, YOLO) and their input normalisation.

det-hlv.name: H1/L1/V1 network
det-hlv.state: Have: H1, L1, V1 for synthetic and real noise. Gap: transient (glitch/event) mode is H1/L1 only; zero-filled missing detectors.

det-new.name: New detectors
det-new.state: Gap: KAGRA, Einstein Telescope, LISA/TianQin/Taiji responses and PSDs (TDI for space).

wf-subst.name: Approximant substitution
wf-subst.state: Have: ripple IMRPhenomD, XAS, Pv2, TaylorF2, D_NRTidalv2. Gap: SEOBNR/EOB, SpinTaylorT4, PhenomPNRT and surrogates are absent; substitute and declare the departure (as the George-Huerta example does) or bridge to LALSimulation.

wf-xphm.name: IMRPhenomXPHM / higher modes
wf-xphm.state: Gap: XPHM deliberately not offered (ripple loses LAL parity at equal masses with spin); MLGWSC-1, Aframe-era and O3 searches use it.

wf-ecc.name: Eccentric / beyond-GR waveforms
wf-ecc.state: Gap: CBCGenerator refuses eccentricity; no ppE/beyond-GR models.

wf-catalogue.name: Waveform-from-file injection
wf-catalogue.state: Gap: injecting numerical waveforms from a catalogue (CCSN simulations, NR, Richers 2017) with sky projection and SNR/HRSS scaling.

wf-pheno-burst.name: Extra burst families
wf-pheno-burst.state: Have: sine-Gaussian, chirplet, ringdown, periodic, WNB, IncoherentGenerator. Gap: Gaussian pulse, cosmic-string cusp, phenomenological CCSN (Astone), scattered-light / whistle shapes, minute-long chirps, magnetar spin-down.

wf-cw.name: Continuous waves
wf-cw.state: Gap: CW signals with Doppler and spin-down over days (LALSuite/PyFstat).

n-real.name: Real GWOSC noise
n-real.state: Have: REAL and PSEUDO_REAL noise O1-O3, flags and vetoes, split by GPS. Gap: real noise is read sequentially (not index-addressed); detectors are always two footprints apart (no coincident mode for training on coincident noise).

n-glitch.name: Gravity Spy glitches
n-glitch.state: Have: TransientDataObtainer with Gravity Spy classes (GlitchType) H1/L1 O1-O3. Gap: glitch-labelled examples mixed as a noise class at set ratios; multi-class labels through ComposedDataset (outside the batch contract).

n-sim-glitch.name: Simulated glitches
n-sim-glitch.state: Gap: single-detector sine-Gaussian/Gaussian/ringdown/scattered-light glitches labelled noise (IncoherentGenerator or a per-detector injection labelled noise).

n-psd-aug.name: PSD augmentation
n-psd-aug.state: Gap: recolouring with sampled PSDs (DINGO, Sage, MLGWSC-1 DS2/DS3); PSEUDO_REAL is the nearest relative.

n-mlgwsc.name: MLGWSC-1 datasets
n-mlgwsc.state: Gap: the challenge's four datasets (DS1-DS4) and its injection/evaluation contract; DS2-DS4 use XPHM with precession and higher modes.

n-external.name: External datasets
n-external.state: Gap: a loader for a published dataset (Gravity Spy Zenodo images, Codabench GWAK, ET MDC, LDC, Richers catalogue).

t-multiclass.name: Multi-class training
t-multiclass.state: Have: ComposedDataset pools and POOL_LABEL. Gap: >2-class heads through the recipe and the batch contract.

t-regression.name: Regression targets
t-regression.state: Have: mass regression (George-Huerta predictor), WaveformParameters labels. Gap: SNR, chirp-mass, time-to-merger and sky targets in the recipe.

t-sequence.name: Per-timestep / dense targets
t-sequence.state: Gap: per-sample or per-pixel labels (WaveNet-style per-timestep classification, U-Net masks, bounding boxes).

t-ae.name: Autoencoder / reconstruction
t-ae.state: Have: WHITENED_INJECTIONS as a clean target. Gap: noise-only reconstruction training and an anomaly-score validator path.

t-curriculum.name: Curricula and schedules
t-curriculum.state: Have: gf.Curriculum (SNR or any Distribution, by epoch). Gap: step/trigger-based curricula, curricula on frequency cutoff or mass, LR schedules beyond Keras.

t-ensemble.name: Ensembles
t-ensemble.state: Gap: training and scoring N independently seeded members, voting and coincidence rules.

t-custom-layer.name: Custom layers
t-custom-layer.state: Gap: layers Keras 3 lacks or the examples do not use: DAIN, GroupNorm (present in Keras), periodic conv, SE/shrinkage, quadratic layer, inception/residual blocks.

t-recurrent.name: Recurrent / attention nets
t-recurrent.state: Have: Keras 3 LSTM/GRU/MultiHeadAttention run on JAX. Gap: none in the library; only example code and memory measurement for long sequences.

t-generative.name: GAN / VAE / flow / Bayesian training
t-generative.state: Gap: custom train steps (WGAN-GP, VAE ELBO, flipout Bayesian layers, normalising flows) under Keras 3 JAX.

t-unsupervised.name: Unsupervised / similarity
t-unsupervised.state: Gap: clustering, contrastive pairs, IIC, UMAP/KDE outlier scoring.

t-nonneural.name: Non-neural models
t-nonneural.state: Gap: trees, GMMs, genetic programming, logistic regression: outside Keras; would need a scikit-learn/XGBoost adapter to the validator.

e-far.name: FAR and efficiency
e-far.state: Have: Validator: exact FAR in Hz with Garwood intervals, efficiency by SNR bin, ROC/AUC, time slides on multi-detector real noise (num_time_slides, cluster_seconds). Gap: streamed continuous-data search with clustering over long stretches.

e-sensitivity.name: Sensitive distance / volume
e-sensitivity.state: Gap: sensitive distance or volume vs FAR over a population (MLGWSC-1 metric), hrss50 for bursts.

e-multiclass.name: Multi-class evaluation
e-multiclass.state: Gap: confusion matrices, per-class accuracy/F1, NMI/ARI for clustering.

e-overlap.name: Waveform overlap
e-overlap.state: Gap: match/overlap of reconstructed vs injected waveform (the matched-filter code has the pieces).

e-events.name: Real events
e-events.state: Have: score_real_events (confident GWTC events, test split). Gap: catalogue masses on event records; O4 events.

e-early.name: Early-warning metrics
e-early.state: Gap: detection time before merger, partial-inspiral SNR labels.

e-pe.name: PE diagnostics
e-pe.state: Gap: P-P plots, JSD against samplers, sky-area metrics.

x-retrieve.name: Full text needed
x-retrieve.state: The paper was not read (paywall or unextractable PDF); the owner or an institutional copy is needed before any adaptation can be stated.

itinerary.title: Retrieve the unread papers
itinerary.why: Nine entries have no architecture at all; their adaptations cannot be stated until the text is read. Cheap for the owner (institutional access), and it unblocks later steps.

itinerary.title: Close the shipped families
itinerary.why: George-Huerta (both nets) and Gabbard are shipped; MLy is shipped without its incoherent and single-detector WNB noise classes. IncoherentGenerator now exists, so MLy's types 2/3 and George-Huerta's real-noise follow-up are the cheapest completions of what is already there.

itinerary.title: 1D CNN ports on the current data path
itinerary.why: Whitened-strain 1D CNNs that need only model code, a declared approximant substitution and at most a multi-class head or longer window. The most cited early literature lives here.

itinerary.title: Search-grade evaluation: sensitive distance and continuous search
itinerary.why: The post-2021 literature reports sensitive distance vs FAR on continuous data with time slides; the validator has FAR and time slides but not sensitive distance or a streamed search. Building this once makes every later CBC entry comparable to MLGWSC-1 and to PyCBC.

itinerary.title: MLGWSC-1 benchmark and its entries
itinerary.why: One benchmark covers AresGW, CNN-Coinc, TPI FSU Jena, MFCNN and is the common yardstick of Aframe, CASTOR, GW-Whisper, Sage and Yamamoto 2025. DS1 is reachable now (non-spinning PhenomD); DS2-DS4 need XPHM, PSD variation and real O3a noise.

itinerary.title: Per-timestep outputs (WaveNet family)
itinerary.why: Gebhard 2019 and the Huerta/Wei WaveNet ensembles emit a score per time step on real noise; one dense-target feature serves all of them and the U-Net segmentation models of step 9.

itinerary.title: Matched-filter front ends
itinerary.why: MatchedFilterLayer and TemplateBank exist; exposing per-template SNR series and SNR maps unlocks MFCNN, Beveridge, McLeod (BNS), Yamamoto 2025, Mobilia and Yan 2021.

itinerary.title: Burst, anomaly and autoencoder models
itinerary.why: Extends MLy: noise-only autoencoders (Moreno, GWAK), generalised-burst training (McGinn), weak supervision (Ratner) and synthetic transient classification (Nigam).

itinerary.title: Denoising and waveform extraction
itinerary.why: Strain-in, clean-waveform-out models trained against WHITENED_INJECTIONS and scored by overlap.

itinerary.title: Time-frequency images and pretrained backbones
itinerary.why: Q-transform/CQT/CWT images and ImageNet backbones serve the ResNet-50 O2/O3 searches, the spectrogram early-warning nets and, in step 10, all of Gravity Spy.

itinerary.title: Glitch classification (Gravity Spy family)
itinerary.why: Twenty-odd glitch papers share one dataset (Gravity Spy) and one input (multi-duration Omega scans). Either a Zenodo image loader or a Q-transform over Gravity Spy times.

itinerary.title: Early warning and long BNS windows
itinerary.why: BNS inspirals need 10-300 s windows, multi-rate inputs, partial-inspiral SNR labels and time-before-merger metrics.

itinerary.title: Core-collapse supernovae and catalogue waveforms
itinerary.why: Supernova detectors need numerical waveforms from files (or Astone's phenomenological model), distance scaling and 3-class heads.

itinerary.title: Exotic training: Bayesian, GAN, VAE, transformers, foundation models
itinerary.why: Each needs a custom train step or heavy pretrained weights; worth doing after the data and evaluation foundations exist.

itinerary.title: Auxiliary-channel and pipeline-coupled models
itinerary.why: DeepClean, iDQ, EMU and cWB-coupled classifiers need non-public channels or an external pipeline; they are reference entries until gravyflow reads auxiliary data.

itinerary.title: Out of core scope: space-based, CW, long transients, skymaps, PE
itinerary.why: Recorded for completeness; each needs a new physics domain.

models.title: Matching matched filtering with deep networks for gravitational-wave astronomy
models.authors: Hunter Gabbard, Michael Williams, Fergus Hayes, Chris Messenger
models.access: Open arXiv (ar5iv).
models.architecture: 1D CNN on 1x8192: 6 conv (8,8,16,16,32,32 filters; kernels 64,32,32,16,16,16), max-pool 8/6/4 after conv 2/4/6 (text says layers 1,5,8: conflict), ELU, dense 64-64 with dropout 0.5, 2-way softmax.
models.inputs: 1 s at 8192 Hz (central 1 s of 2 s, Tukey 1/8), whitened by aLIGO design PSD; merger at 0.75-0.95 of the window.
models.data: Gaussian noise (aLIGO design). IMRPhenomD non-spinning BBH, 5-95 Msun log-uniform, isotropic. One dataset per optimal SNR (1-10); 4e5 series, 50/50, 25 noise realisations per signal, 90/5/5.
models.training: Binary cross-entropy; Nadam lr 0.002 (beta 0.9/0.999, eps 1e-8, schedule 0.004); TensorFlow. Batch, epochs not stated.
models.results: ROC and efficiency at FAP 1e-1..1e-3 vs a PyCBC bank (8056 templates): 'closely matches' matched filtering; no numeric AUC.
models.code: None stated. Thesis and gravyflow implementations exist.
models.gaps: Batch, epochs, strides/padding, pooling placement conflict, waveform-count conflict (1000 vs ~8000).
models.adaptation_notes: Shipped (Gabbard2017, 41,842 weights at the CPU preset's 2048 Hz). The paper's per-SNR-tailored training is a config sweep of the shipped recipe.

comparability.what_differs: Per-SNR balanced test sets of 1 s windows in Gaussian aLIGO-design noise, non-spinning BBH; FAP is per window, so no rate. The paired matched-filter curve on identical data is the paper's comparison.
highlighted_errors: CNN above the matched filter at FAP 0.1 for rho 3-5 (Fig 3) is not possible for an optimal filter in Gaussian noise; the bank or threshold handling is suspect.
Waveform count conflict: 4e5 series with 25 noise draws each implies 8000 signals, the text says 1000.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Best comparison to MF available: matched efficiency curves vs optimal SNR at FAP 1e-1,1e-2,1e-3 on balanced per-SNR test sets in Gaussian noise. FAP is the fraction of noise-only 1-s samples above threshold, not a rate (needs a time-per-sample conversion; 1-s windows -> FAP 1e-3 ~ 1e-3/s ~ 86/day without clustering). 'SNR' is optimal SNR of a single detector inside the central 1 s; one CNN per SNR (trained at that SNR) so efficiency curves are from networks trained at different SNRs, not one network swept in SNR. MF given only a 0.75-0.95 peak window, flat priors, so comparison is conditioned on those.
suspected_errors_extracted: Within-paper tension: matched filtering is optimal in Gaussian noise, yet Fig. 3 shows the CNN above the MF at FAP=0.1 for rho=3-5 (e.g. rho=4: CNN ~0.44 vs MF ~0.305) and at FAP 0.01 for rho=4 (0.16 vs 0.10). Likely cause: CNN is trained on the restricted prior (peak window, mass range) while the MF stat maximises over all times and templates (trials factor); not stated, so MF/CNN not like for like.
Dataset size: training set 4e5 time series, 50% signals, 25 noise realisations per signal implies 8000 unique waveforms, but the text says 1000 unique waveforms in total (1000x25=25,000, not 2e5).
Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 y-axis is called 'true alarm probability' and x 'false alarm probability' (conventional terms are TPR and FPR); no error in numbers.

models.architecture: Two dilated 1D CNNs, each trained as a mass predictor then converted to a 2-class classifier. Small (~2 MB): 3 conv (16/32/64 filters, kernels 16/8/8, dilation 4 in the last two), max-pool 4/4 after each, 2 FC. Deep (~23 MB): 4 conv (kernels 16/16/16/32, dilations 1/2/2/2), pool 4, 3 FC. models.comparability_notes_extractor: NOT a compact-binary search: the signal is a damped sinusoid in white Gaussian noise with a 0.03 s detection window (catalogue notes the thesis one-liner saying BBH is wrong). FPR is a per-sample false positive rate over ~95,000 noise windows, not a rate per time. Quoted headline numbers are at rho_opt=2, using the paper's own optimal-SNR convention (Eq. 2, printed with a factor 2 rather than the usual 4 and with a PSD of the data), so SNR is not comparable with other papers. Matched-filter baseline is a bank of the 25,000 training waveforms, a non-standard weak baseline.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Table 3: SE5 sensitivity 0.947 at FPR=1e-3 for rho_opt=2; text: CNN much more sensitive than matched filtering (Fig. 7)
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: For a known signal in Gaussian noise, the Neyman-Pearson bound (matched filter) at rho=2 and FPR=1e-3 is Phi(2-3.09)=0.14, and a 25,000-template bank can only lower it. 0.947 is far above that unless the paper rho_opt is defined with a different normalisation (Eq. 2 prints a factor 2 and the text says ratio of max amplitude to noise sigma for A_S/N) or the CNN exploits a data artifact (e.g. fixed t0 windows, signal energy outside the stated band). A CNN cannot beat the optimal detector at a true SNR of 2.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Table 1: Test set 1 t0 range [0,0.026] s versus training [0,0.03] s; SE1 uses a 1 s window
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: SE1 (1 s window, 8192 Hz) is trained on Training set 2 with t0 in [0,1], but the Table 3 caption refers to subsets of Test set 1_1 and 2_1; which test set each row uses is ambiguous, so SE1-SE5 may not be evaluated on identical data.

Real-event tests give per-frame counts (7 false detections in 150 frames at conf 0.5) but only on two events. Precision/recall depend on the object/background ratio and confidence threshold (not stated for P/R in Table III), so they are not comparable to TPR at a fixed FAR; mAP is not a GW-search metric. No result below SNR 10.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: mAP0.5:0.95 vs mAP0.5 gap
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Table III 20/80: mAP0.5=0.890, mAP0.5:0.95=0.855, i.e. almost no loss over IoU thresholds up to 0.95, unusually flat; boxes come from injection extent (analytic boxes), so label noise/size is large. Possible but should be treated with care.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Conclusion says GW170817 detected "in both H1 and L1"
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Sec V C: L1 detection required an ad hoc cap of spectrogram values at 256 applied after the failure was seen; raw L1 data gave no detection.

models.title: Ensemble of deep convolutional neural networks for real-time gravitational wave signal recognition
models.authors: CunLiang Ma, Wei Wang, He Wang, Zhoujian Cao
models.access: Open arXiv (ar5iv).
models.architecture: Gabbard-style base learner on 1x4096: conv 8, 8, pool; 16, 16, pool; 32, 32, pool; flatten 352; Dense 64 + dropout x2; softmax 2; ELU. Bagging: 100 learners per detector, top 10 by val AUC, soft voting (arithmetic or harmonic mean); trigger needs >5 consecutive alerts in both detectors.
models.inputs: H1, L1; 1 s at 4096 Hz stepped 1/8 s; whitened, 20 Hz high-pass.
models.data: ggwd EOBNR BBH 5-80 Msun, spin 0-0.998, network SNR 7-20; real O1 noise without events. 120k generated; train 60k, val 10k, test 50k; 100 bootstrap sets.
models.training: Nadam lr 0.002, batch 32, Keras, 1080 Ti; loss and epochs not stated.
models.results: 9 of 10 O1/O2 BBH recovered (GW170818 missed); estimated FAR ~1 per 11.24 days; merger time error <0.1 s; <2 ms latency.
models.code: ggwd only.
models.gaps: Kernel sizes (derivable from shapes), dropout rate, loss, epochs.
models.adaptation_notes: Gabbard2017-like base learner with derived kernels; bagging over seeds; real O1 noise; per-detector sub-ensembles and consecutive-alert coincidence on a streamed scan.

comparability.what_differs: Per-window FAP on a bespoke 20 %-signal test set in O1 noise; the "1 per 11.24 days" FAR is extrapolated by multiplying H and L probabilities.
highlighted_errors: The coincident FAR assumes independent, exactly simultaneous H and L false triggers.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Metrics are FAP per 1 s window on a bespoke ggwd test set (20% signals, SNR 7-20 network, single-detector per sub-ensemble); not an ROC AUC or accuracy. The FAR 1 per 11.24 days is derived by extrapolation from per-detector false-trigger rates assuming independence and zero-lag coincidence of triggers (no light-travel-time window), not measured from time slides. Detection counts apply to 10 loud BBH events with O1-only training. TAP/FAP are not at a stated SNR so cannot be compared with SNR-binned efficiencies. Only a ROC range FAP in [0,0.02] is shown, so no AUC.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Detected-count vs ROC tension
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: At the threshold with FAP=0.004, Livingston TAP should be >=0.8 (Fig 5b gives TAP=0.8 already at FAP 0.0012), yet only 7851 detections are quoted for Livingston step 1/8 s (and 8711 for Hanford) out of 10,000 test signals (denominator not stated); 78.5% < 80%. Possibly because detection requires >5 consecutive alerts, but the paper does not say.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Independence assumption in FAR
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: pf = pfH x pfL assumes H and L false triggers are independent and exactly simultaneous; the physical coincidence window (10 ms) and non-Gaussian correlated glitches are ignored, and no false trigger was seen, so the 1/11.24 d is a model estimate (expected 1 event in 17 d).

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Test set mismatch
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Model trained and tested on ggwd-injected signals with network SNR range 7-20 in O1 noise; GW170818 (H SNR 4.1) missed consistent with lowest training SNR 7.

models.title: MLGWSC-1: The first Machine Learning Gravitational-Wave Search Mock Data Challenge
models.authors: Marlin B. Schafer, Ondrej Zelenka, Alexander H. Nitz, et al.
models.venue: preprint (later Phys. Rev. D 107, 023021 (2023), from memory, unverified)
models.access: Open arXiv (ar5iv; last ~45k chars unread).
models.architecture: A benchmark, not a model. Entries: MFCNN (learnable templates + MobileNetV3), CNN-Coinc (schafer2021b), TPI FSU Jena (deeper CNN, two-detector, USR), Virgo-AUTh (AresGW, nousi2022), PyCBC, cWB.
models.inputs: H1+L1 2048 Hz, >=2 h segments, 15 Hz cutoff; submissions are executables returning (time, stat, var).
models.data: DS1 Gaussian aLIGO ZDHP, non-spinning BBH 10-50 Msun no HOM; DS2 20 O3a-derived PSDs, aligned spins; DS3 per-segment random PSD, precession + 10 modes; DS4 real O3a (~81 d coincident), L1 shifted. All IMRPhenomXPHM, chirp distance uniform in d^2 130-350 Mpc, mergers 24-30 s apart.
models.training: Per entry.
models.results: Sensitive distance at 1/month: DS1 PyCBC 2491, TPI 2362, AUTh 2116; DS4 PyCBC 1544, AUTh 1092, CNN-Coinc and TPI 0. Best ML ~95% of PyCBC (DS1), ~70% (DS4).
models.code: github.com/gwastro/ml-mock-data-challenge-1 (verified).
models.gaps: Appendices unread.
models.adaptation_notes: Implement the challenge's data generator (or read its released files) and its evaluation contract (FAR = N_FP / T over 30 d, injection found within var, chirp-mass-weighted sensitive volume). DS1 is feasible with IMRPhenomD now; DS2-DS4 need XPHM and PSD variation.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: The benchmark designed for comparability: all entries evaluated by one contract (FAR in 1/month, sensitive distance in Mpc, 1 month test data). Only the four BBH datasets with IMRPhenomXPHM, chirp distance 130-350 Mpc, BBH only (DS1 10-50 Msun; no sub-solar, no BNS), 15 Hz cutoff. Sensitive distance values are exact (Table IV) so they can be used as the gold anchor to compare reproductions. Fig 2 curves also contain FAR>100/month but are not tabulated. FARs <1/month were not evaluated, so extrapolating to astrophysical thresholds needs care. PyCBC DS1 used a smaller bank than DS2-4.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Real L1 noise but only the Gaussian-like quiet stretches used (no known events or hardware injections); 4 s windows, single detector, zero-spin, 4-class (noise/BBH/BNS/NSBH) softmax. Reported TAP is at FAP per 0.2 s segment (1e-3 ~ authors say 1e3 per month, probably ~1e4 per month), so the false-alarm level is orders of magnitude looser than MLGWSC-1 (1/month): not comparable with FAR-based sensitive distances. The metric of interest is SNR at which TAP saturates (BBH 8, NSBH 10, BNS 13 at FAP 1e-3). Test set uses SNR uniform in 1-20, in-distribution with training (not distance-based). Real-event recovery uses the highest-SNR detector only and counts classification, not detection significance.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: FAR conversion looks too small: FAP 1e-3 per 0.2 s segment on one month (1.3e7 segments) gives ~1.3e4 false alarms per month, not ~1e3 as stated; also the text says "FAR of 0.1%" which is a probability, not a rate.

models.training: 50 epochs, batch 50, lr 1e-4; optimiser, loss, framework not stated.
models.results: Stage I >99%; aligned vs precessing ~91%; 3-class ~94%; 498/500 injections found in continuous data; GWTC events with SNR>=13 detected.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: No injection-based sensitivity (TPR at fixed FAR, sensitive distance) is reported for the upgraded model; injections are used only to fit the foreground exponent for p_astro. Efficiency is counted as events recovered with p_astro>0.5 in a catalogue-matched range, so it is not comparable with MLGWSC-1 sensitive-volume at FAR=1/month. The 'surpasses traditional pipelines' claim compares published-pipeline counts against AresGW counts that include its own 8 unvalidated candidates (34 vs 36 for GWTC pipelines on published events alone, 34 vs 37 for OGC), applies a hand-chosen chirp-mass cut (10-40 Msun) and uses a FAR from O3a-only time shifts (conservative for O3b). Ranking statistic Rs saturates at 16 (1e-16 regulariser). Triggers pass visual inspection and Gravity Spy glitch removal before p_astro, so the FARs are post-veto. Training noise overlaps the O3a test data (mitigated by 40% shuffling).

comparability.what_differs: Real O3 noise and the official GWTC-3 BNS injection set: directly comparable with the LVK pipelines on that set.
highlighted_errors: Fig 7 caption names week 3 (the background week) as the injection week.
GW170817 FAR 6.9e-13 Hz is a Gaussian-tail extrapolation from a background reaching 1.8e-8 Hz.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Sensitive distance vs FAR on the official GWTC-3 O3 BNS injection set (2,800 injections, week 4) is comparable with the offline pipelines (distances read from Fig 7, +-4 Mpc) and with MLGWSC-style sensitive distances only after matching weighting. BNS-only search; offline pipelines search BBH/NSBH/BNS, a ~10% volume handicap the authors quantify. The 34% found fraction is for the injection distribution including distant (SNR>=6) events, so not an efficiency at fixed SNR. FAR for GW170817 relies on a Gaussian-tail extrapolation beyond 0.56/yr.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Figure 7 caption vs text
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Fig 7 caption says 'third week of the O3 injection run' but Sec V.A states the third week was used for background and the fourth week was the injection run; likely a caption error.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Extrapolated FARs
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: GW170817 FAR 6.9e-13 Hz is from a Gaussian fit to the tail (R^2=0.984) of a background reaching only 1.77e-8 Hz; the authors give a 1.7e-12 to 2.4e-14 band. Not a measured FAR.

models.title: Identifying and Mitigating Machine Learning Biases for the Gravitational Wave Detection Problem (Sage)
models.authors: Narenraju Nagarajan et al.
models.access: Open arXiv (HTML; only the first 100k of 234k chars read; architecture section truncated).
models.architecture: Per-detector multiscale frontend (OSNet-inspired residual, large kernels) + attention backend; InstanceNorm. Sizes not obtained.
models.inputs: H1+L1, 12 s windows with multirate sampling (2048 Hz near merger, down to 128 Hz); median-PSD whitening scaled to [-1,1].
models.data: O3b (~114 d) + MLGWSC-1 O3a days 36-81 noise; IMRPhenomPv2 on the fly uniform in tau0/tau3; SNR >=5 skewed low; PSD recolouring with 250,000 PSDs at 40%.
models.training: BCE + MSE on t_c and chirp mass; Adam lr 2e-4, wd 1e-6, cosine warm restarts; batch 64; grad clip 1.
models.results: MLGWSC-1 DS4 at 1/month: ~11.2% more signals than PyCBC, ~48% more than the previous best ML.
models.code: github.com/nnarenraju/sage (from paper).
models.gaps: Architecture (re-read from offset 100000), epochs, hardware.
models.adaptation_notes: Multirate 12 s windows and PSD recolouring are the two new features; IMRPhenomPv2 native.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Uses MLGWSC-1 D4 (30-day real O3a, 1-month) evaluation: sensitive distance at FAR 1/month directly comparable with the other MLGWSC-1 entries (AresGW, Aframe, TPI-FSU Jena, MFCNN, PyCBC, cWB), taken from the Table V. The best result (Sage-Broad) uses PSDs from the test period to recolour the training noise (acknowledged mild train/test overlap, Sec V) and takes the best of 3 seeds in the table (mean is lower, Fig 11). Aframe and TPI-FSU Jena numbers come by private communication. PyCBC compared with a different mass distribution (tau0-tau3 vs U(m1,m2)). The paper itself argues the sensitive-distance metric is biased toward high chirp mass, so counts of found injections are given alongside. Only 1 month background: FAR floor 1/month.

models.title: A Search for Binary Black Hole Mergers in LIGO O1-O3 Data with Convolutional Neural Networks
models.authors: Ethan Silver et al.
models.access: Open arXiv (HTML).
models.architecture: Ensemble: time-series CNN (Krastev-like: conv 32/64/128/256, kernels 16/8/8/8, pool 4, dense 128, 64, softmax), time-series ResNet (3.86M params), 2D CNN/ResNet on 300x300 Q-transforms; plus a chirp-mass regressor.
models.inputs: H1+L1, 4096 Hz, 4 s; Welch-whitened; Q-transform 30-330 Hz of the last 0.5 s for 2D models.
models.data: ~22 d of O2 noise; SEOBNRv4 non-spinning up to 150 Msun, q<=10; SNR 7-20; hard negatives (one-detector signals, mismatched chirp mass, time offsets >50 ms); 480,000 training templates.
models.training: Sparse CE; Adam AMSGrad lr 1e-3; batch 216; 200 epochs; TF; 4 A100.
models.results: 57 of 75 GWTC-3 BBH found (41 with no false positives at a stricter cut); ~100 yr time-shifted background; compared with AresGW and Aframe.
models.code: Not stated (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10473621 in references, unverified).
models.gaps: Strides, schedule, test size.
models.adaptation_notes: Time-series members are step-2 ports; hard-negative classes need IncoherentGenerator-style mismatched injections labelled noise; 2D members wait for Q-transforms.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Real-data event-recovery search with time-slide FAR; a different task from fixed-FAR injection efficiency. No ROC, accuracy or sensitive-distance numbers. Operating point (57 TPs / 57 FPs) is at tens of false alarms per year, far above LVK-style 1/yr or 1/month thresholds, so event counts are not comparable with AresGW/Aframe at p_astro>0.5 without matching FAR. Only graphical efficiency vs (SNR, mass), at an unstated FAR. Models were thresholded using the same GWTC-3 events they are scored on.
suspected_errors_extracted: Sec III B counts as true positives the catalogue events the pipeline recovers, and describes false positives as the events the pipeline fails to detect. Read literally, this makes the false positives the 18 missed events, which contradicts the 57 false positives given elsewhere; the intended meaning is almost certainly candidates that are not in the catalogue.
Thresholds for every ensemble member were set from performance in the real GWTC-3 search (Table I note), so 57/75 is a tuned in-sample figure, not a held-out one.
Two stated event counts coexist (57/75 over O1-O3 and 49/65 in the O3-only comparison) and use different subsets; GW200129_065458 was added by hand despite a DQ flag.
Extrapolated FARs (e.g. 1/350,000 yr) use a power-law fit extrapolated far beyond ~100 yr of shifted background.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Efficiency is the fraction of injections recovered over a hrss grid (N=0..8 in steps of sqrt(3)) at a given FAR in 1/yr, so it depends on the injection amplitude distribution and is not a sensitive distance or sensitive volume; ROC curves are per waveform family. Standard cWB is penalised by a 3-bin trials factor in the comparison (the paper notes this). Requires cWB trigger production, so it is a post-processing stage, not a standalone detector. Fig. 3 (CCSN efficiencies, ~0.05-0.45) was not read numerically.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Training/test split of the background
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Sec III B: 70% of noise background for training and the rest (30%) for testing; Sec IV: maximum test background 200 yr because 20% of the 1000 yr background was used as test data. 30% vs 20% inconsistent (300 yr vs 200 yr).

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Waveform label GP in Table III versus GA in text and figures
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Table III lists Gaussian Pulse (GP) rows 17-20; the rest of the paper calls them GA (GA0d1 etc.).

models.title: Source-agnostic gravitational-wave detection with recurrent autoencoders
models.authors: Eric A. Moreno, Bartlomiej Borzyszkowski, Maurizio Pierini, Jean-Roch Vlimant, Maria Spiropulu
models.access: Open arXiv (ar5iv).
models.architecture: LSTM-AE / GRU-AE: 256 windows of (100,1); encoder 32, 8; RepeatVector; decoder 8, 32 + per-step Dense; MSE. CNN-AE: Conv1D 256, 128 k3 + pool, mirrored. Supervised CNN benchmark.
models.inputs: Simulated L1+H1 at 2048 Hz, 8 s cropped to 2.5 s; aLIGO ZDHP; whitened, 30 Hz-2048 Hz, scaled to [0,1].
models.data: 400,000 noise samples (64/16/20); BBH SEOBNRv4 10-80 Msun and BNS IMRPhenomDNRTidal_v2, SNR 5-20 for evaluation only.
models.training: MSE; optimiser, lr, batch, epochs not stated.
models.results: Single-detector TPR at FPR 0.1/0.01: LSTM-AE BBH 46.1/30.4%, BNS 23.7/11.4%. The thesis's 'FAR 0.01 Hz' is an FPR fraction.
models.code: Datasets on Zenodo (refs 44, 45); ggwd; model code not stated.
models.gaps: Optimiser, lr, latent size, thresholds.
models.adaptation_notes: Noise-only reconstruction training and a reconstruction-error score in the validator; LSTM layers are native Keras; signals only at evaluation (IMRPhenomD/D_NRTidalv2 native).

Classification among 10 classes at fixed distance, whitened STFT + three-detector input; accuracy depends on distance (hence SNR) and is dominated by the easy m39 class at large distance. Noise recall 0.96-0.97 corresponds to a 3-4% per-sample false-positive fraction, orders of magnitude above GW FAR standards; no FAR, ROC or detection-efficiency-at-FAR is given. models.architecture: Model 1 (coincidence): 3 residual blocks of 2 conv (64 then 128 filters), ReLU+BN, GAP, dense+BN, softmax. Model 2 (coherence): strain branch (3 conv, GAP) + correlation branch (2 conv over 60-lag Pearson per pair), concatenated, dense. Combined score = product.

Fig 4 background uses "1 month" of data but the tuning FAR is 1/day while headline results use 1/yr; the 1/yr threshold relies on ~1e3 time lags of days to weeks of data, i.e. it is a time-lag extrapolation, not an independently measured 1/yr rate.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Burst detector for CCSN waveforms in simulated Gaussian noise (single detector, O4 design PSD); the metric is the 10/50/90% exclusion distance in kpc for galactic CCSNe at a false-alarm level of one background event per 5 simulated years (efficiency vs the loudest background event, so a FAP-based, not time-resolved, threshold). Not comparable to BBH/CBC sensitive distances (Mpc) or MLGWSC-1; comparable only to other CCSN/burst searches reporting a CCSN distance reach at a stated FAR (e.g. hrss-based or cWB distances) if the waveforms and noise PSD match. Waveform-dependent (m39 4x further than s18), no real data, no glitches.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Table I columns are labelled 10%, 50%, 90% exclusion distance but the values decrease from 10% to 90% (e.g. mesa20_pert 0.26/0.15/0.06 kpc); the convention (distance at which efficiency is 10/50/90%) is defined only in the Fig 6 caption, not in the table caption. Table matches Fig 6 for s18 (0.16/0.64/1.25 kpc read off the dots) so it is consistent.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Burst/unmodelled search with FAR in per-day units (not per-month) on its own 2.98-d simulated (Gaussian, injections span BBH/BHNS/BNS/glitch/CCSN) and 2.16-d real O4b sets; efficiency vs FAR, not sensitive distance, so NOT comparable with MLGWSC-1 results. Real-data efficiencies are for injections only, with injections of arbitrary SNR 8-100 and mass distributions of its own. 1/month FAR yields zero recall on real O4, so the pipeline is not operating at the standard 1/month threshold. AUCs are depressed by the coincidence ceiling.
suspected_errors_extracted: Sec. V B.2 says the GNN leads Rmor "at every rate the background resolves", but on real O4 (Table III) Rmor beats the GNN for BNS at 100/day (0.21 vs 0.17) and 1000/day (0.25 vs 0.23).

AUCs in Fig. 7 (e.g. BNS 0.06, SNR 8-12 band 0.18-0.20) are far below 0.5 because curves saturate at the fraction admitted in coincidence; they are not discrimination AUCs and must not be compared with AUCs of other papers.
Real-O4 efficiency at 1/month is zero in every class and at 1/day is 0.28 (all), versus 0.70 on the simulated set; summaries stating "similar gains on real O4" understate the simulated-to-real drop.

Table II/Fig. 4 simulated n (3310, 289, 201, 190) differs from injected counts in the text (3349 BBH, 258 BH-NS, 193 BNS) and from real-set n (3281...): the simulated BH-NS n (289) exceeds the 258 injected, which is unexplained.

models.authors: Daniel Ratner
models.access: Open arXiv (HTML). Single author per text (catalogue says 'et al.').
models.architecture: Small 2D CNN (2,139 params, shared H/L weights): three 3x3 conv, flatten 312, dropout 0.05, Linear 6, 6, 3.
models.inputs: H and L streams, 50 ms windows of Codabench GWAK challenge data; STFT window 128, overlap 96; content above 1.6 kHz dropped.

models.results: SGLF 100 events at 0.2%: PR-AUC 0.89, recall 0.86 (supervised baseline 0.86/0.83); BBH 0.91/0.88.
models.code: Not stated.
models.gaps: Sample rate, whitening, SNR range.
models.adaptation_notes: Either load the Codabench dataset or regenerate it (raikman2023's priors); custom coincidence loss on paired detector outputs.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Evaluated on the CodaBench anomaly-detection challenge data: 50 ms windows of cleaned real LIGO noise (static, no glitches) with injected BBH or SGLF signals, SNR taken from a separate 10k-signal subset, not a continuous-strain search. Metrics are PR-AUC and recall at <=1 false alarm per year, where the FAR is not measured on time-slid strain but estimated from single-channel false-positive probabilities squared under a detector-independence assumption with 50k backgrounds; training uses an enriched event rate (0.2% via trigger). Not comparable with MLGWSC-1 sensitive distance or with real-data FAR estimates (no glitches). Comparable only to other CodaBench/GWAK-style anomaly benchmarks at the same event rate, and with Raikman 2023 (GWAK) in terms of recall vs SNR at FAR 1/yr only qualitatively.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Abstract quotes recall up to 0.91 (BBH) and 0.85 (SGLF) at FAR 1/yr, but Table I gives BBH PR-AUC 0.91 and recall 0.88, SGLF recall 0.86 (PR-AUC 0.89); the abstract number 0.91 is the PR-AUC and 0.85 matches no table entry.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: FAR 1/yr is derived by squaring a single-channel false-positive probability from only 50k backgrounds (assuming H/L independence) and extrapolating by ~3e8 windows/yr; precision at those levels is an extrapolation of 5-6 orders of magnitude beyond the data, and the 0.02% training rate dataset resamples the same 50k backgrounds.

models.title: GWAK: Gravitational-Wave Anomalous Knowledge with Recurrent Autoencoders
models.authors: Ryan Raikman, Eric A. Moreno, Ekaterina Govorkova, et al.
models.access: Open arXiv (HTML).
models.architecture: Five AEs: LSTM AEs for BBH, SG 64-512 Hz, SG 512-1024 Hz (bottlenecks 4, 8, 8; ~510k params each); fully connected AEs for background and glitches (~242k). 12 features (per-AE detector reconstruction overlaps + frequency-domain H.L + Pearson; text also says 7/10) -> linear SVM score.
models.inputs: H1+L1 O3a, 4096 Hz, whitened against 1 h of background, 30-1500 Hz; AE inputs 200 points (50 ms), unit std.
models.data: Background 80k/10k/10k; Omicron glitches same; BBH IMRPhenomPv2 (5-100 Msun) and SG injections with 5-step SNR curriculum; classifier on 6 classes incl. WNB and a supernova (85 Msun, SFHo).
models.training: MAE; signal AEs reconstruct the clean template; Adam reset per curriculum step; 200 epochs.
models.results: Supernova at ~SNR 22 for <=1 false event/hour; similar to MLy on BBH and SG, lower on WNB and supernova.
models.code: github.com/ML4GW/gwak (verified).
models.gaps: Layer detail, lr, batch.
models.adaptation_notes: Clean-template reconstruction targets (WHITENED_INJECTIONS), per-class AE training, frequency-domain correlation features, Gravity Spy glitches in place of Omicron triggers (declared). Supernova class needs one catalogue waveform.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Anomaly-detection pipeline evaluated on injections into one hour or so of real O3a H1+L1 noise; FAR from 1 yr of time slides, efficiency vs optimal SNR (not distance) at FAR 1/yr and at 1/hr-1/month. Comparable to other burst/unmodelled searches (MLy, cWB) only at matched FAR and SNR definition: SNR here is injected network-optimal SNR, with SG and WNB morphology specific to this paper (WNB duration 0.1 s; supernova a single waveform). No hrss50 or distance reach. BBH efficiency 50% at SNR ~15.5 at FAR 1/yr is far worse than a matched-filter search; the BBH metric is not comparable with CBC sensitive distance at 1/month. Training noise limited to ~71 min from the beginning of O3a.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Supernova result quoted two ways: text says 1 false event per hour at SNR ~22, Fig 12 text says FAR 1-2 per month at SNR 20-25, and Fig 13 (FAR 1/year) shows 50% efficiency only at SNR ~27: three different FAR/SNR pairings for supernova, only one of which (hourly) is "alert-ready"; summary in the catalogue (SNR 22 for <=1 false event/hour) corresponds to the loosest FAR.
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Sec 4.3 p19, Sec 4.4 p21, Fig 13 p22

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Fig 11 caption says WNB drops to FAR below one per year while the text for the supernova panel says one or fewer per month; both are single events, so the numbers are illustrative only.

Data span GPS 1238166018-1238170289 is only ~4271 s (~71 min) yet the text implies training and 1 yr of timeslides can be built; timeslide background of 1 yr from ~71 min needs ~1e5 shifts, so the FAR 1/yr is extrapolated from heavily reused data (not stated).

models.title: Pre-trained Audio Transformer as a Foundational AI Tool for Gravitational Waves (GW-Whisper)
models.authors: Chayan Chatterjee et al.
models.access: Open arXiv (HTML; first 100k of 107k chars).
models.architecture: Whisper-tiny encoder (paper also says 24 layers: conflict) behind a Q-transform adapter (3 conv-ReLU-pool), resize to 80x3000, detector FiLM; DoRA rank-8 fine-tuning (~196k trainable of ~39M); MLP head (two conflicting specs).
models.inputs: H1+L1 (detection), single detector (glitches); 2048 Hz, 1 s windows stride 0.1 s; log-mel features for glitches.
models.data: IMRPhenomXPHM BBH 10-50 Msun, SNR 7-20; Gravity Spy 9 classes + no-glitch (p>90%, SNR>=8).
models.training: BCE / CE / contrastive NCE pre-training; optimiser, lr, epochs not stated; DGX A100.
models.results: MLGWSC-1 DS3/DS4 ~900 Mpc at 1/month; O3b 18 of 31 BBH; glitch accuracy 94-98% per class.
models.code: Stated available; URL not in text.
models.gaps: Optimiser, lr, sizes, head conflict.
models.adaptation_notes: Whisper weights and DoRA under Keras 3 JAX (KerasHub has Whisper; DoRA would be custom), a Q-transform adapter input, MLGWSC-1 evaluation.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Toy-scale test: 10 loud catalogue events vs 10 noise samples (n=20), so AUC 0.89 carries a binomial uncertainty of roughly +-0.08-0.1. No FAR, no SNR stratification, no injection set, no real-data background beyond 10 samples. Signal samples are loud public events (cut around the event time), not blind search. Comparable only to other anomaly-detection AUCs on event-vs-noise tests; not comparable with TPR-at-FAR numbers.
suspected_errors_extracted: Sample size/time: text says a sample is 4 s at 4 kHz per detector, 'Each sample is 4x4000 = 16000 entries' for two detectors (two detectors x 4 s x 4000 Hz would be 32000); the 16000 matches one detector, or 4 kHz x 2 s x 2 detectors; ambiguous.
Fig. 2 shows GW150914 at t=16.5 s of the strain segment while Fig. 5 shows its loss spike at t=4 s of an 8-s plot (different segment cuts, not stated).

The paper claims AUC > 0.7 indicates better performance; AUC 0.89 from 10 vs 10 samples is statistically weak (no error bar); F1 0.857 is consistent with TP=9,FN=1,FP=2 or similar but the threshold is not given.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Anomaly detector on ET mock data, single channel, no antenna pattern, Gaussian noise (no glitches): FAR is a nominal Gaussian-tail statement assuming independent 2-s segments, not an empirical background count. Efficiency is per-injected-IMBH mergers at very large distances (10-40 Gpc-scale injections / MDC SNR) and is not a distance reach; no sensitive distance, ROC or AUC. Not comparable with LIGO-data FAR/volume metrics.
suspected_errors_extracted: Abstract/Sec 4.1 give FAR 4.5/yr; Conclusions give 4.6/yr.

The 5-sigma threshold actually used (MSE 0.005) is ~6.3 sigma on the fitted Gaussian (mu+5 sigma = 0.0045): the quoted FAR of 4.5/yr corresponds to the Gaussian 5-sigma, whereas the threshold is set from a Pareto tail fit; FAR not verified empirically (only ~1 month of data, so 4.5/yr cannot be measured).

Weakly supervised training injections (80-150 Msun, 10-40 Gpc, IMRPhenomPv2) overlap in parameter space with the IMBH test set (MDC masses ~100-200), so '100% recovery' is partially in-distribution; number of IMBH test mergers not stated.
Two-detector FAR (1.3e-6/yr) simply squares per-segment probabilities, ignoring coincidence window and non-Gaussian tails, which the paper itself says are heavier than Gaussian.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Simulated-only (no real LIGO strain, leading-order Newtonian waveform, no antenna pattern, N_det=3 folded into distance). 'FAR' is the fraction of 256 s null segments flagged (dimensionless), convertible to Hz (0.01 -> 3.9e-5 Hz = 1/7.1 h) but the lowest FAR probed is ~3e-4 per segment (~1 per 9 d); minimum FAR here is far above GW-search FARs (1/month to 1/year), so the numbers are not comparable to matched-filter or other ML FAR figures without rescaling. Sensitivity is in effective distance with 3 detectors folded in, 1.4+1.4 BNS at f_cut=25 Hz (early warning ~87 s), not the standard sensitive distance. Early-warning (partial inspiral) task, so TAR/ROC are not comparable to full-signal CBC detection papers.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Multi-class glitch classification on Omega-scan images, not detection: no FAR, ROC or AUC. Labels were partly produced by earlier ML + volunteers, so label noise is shared with the training data.
suspected_errors_extracted: The Fig. 7 caption says the confusion matrix is normalised by each class's glitch count in the training set, but its title says it shows the testing set. The printed rows each sum to 1.0 per test class, so the normalisation uses test-class counts and the caption is wrong or misleading.

'Average accuracy 97.1%' does not equal the mean of the printed per-class recalls (~0.90); it must be the sample-weighted overall accuracy. A reader taking it as macro accuracy would overstate performance on rare classes.

Possible count inconsistency: text says Wandering Line has 44 and Paired Doves 30 samples (whole set); Wandering Line recalls 0.57/0.43 imply ~7 test samples (4/7, 3/7), more than the 12.5% share (~5.5) of 44; unresolved (Table 1 is an image and not read).

Dataset size ~8500 here vs 7932 samples (22 classes) given for the updated Gravity Spy O1 set by Glanzer et al. 2023 (their Sec 2.3): unexplained 7% difference.
'Narrowed to within 5 classes with 100.00% confidence' is an overstatement of a top-5 accuracy of 100.00% on ~1700 samples (VGG16 99.88%).

models.comparability_notes_extractor: The 90.9% is NOT a standard accuracy: it is a custom label-purity measure over 36 unsupervised clusters (vs 22 labels), computed on the training data, with C chosen using the label-based accuracy. Purity-style scores rise with the number of clusters, so it cannot be compared with the 97.1% supervised accuracy or other supervised numbers. No precision/recall/F1 (the paper says they are ill-defined for a non-square confusion matrix). No FAR concept.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Equation (1) as printed sums max(v_i)/|v_i|_1 over clusters i=1..C with no weighting by cluster size or division by C, which would give a value up to 36, not a fraction; the intended definition is presumably the size-weighted purity sum_i max(v_i) / sum_i |v_i|_1.
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Discussion, Eq. (1), p6.

suspected_errors_extracted.issue: Hyperparameters (C=36, K=5) are stated to be 'the optimal performance ... using the accuracy', i.e. selected with labels on the evaluation data, so 90.9% is optimistic and not a blind result.

Accuracy of 93.5% includes a simulated 'real' class while the actual O3 retraction test is only 10/22 (45%) correct: the headline accuracy overstates real-world noise rejection.

models.title: Generalised gravitational wave burst generation with generative adversarial networks (McGANn)
models.authors: J. McGinn, C. Messenger, M. J. Williams, I. S. Heng
models.access: Open arXiv (ar5iv).
models.architecture: Conditional DCGAN: generator Dense 32768 -> 4 transposed conv (k18 s2); discriminator 4 conv (k14 s2), LeakyReLU, spatial dropout 0.5. Evaluation CNN: H1+L1 1024x2, 4 conv (k5 s2, 8 filters), Dense 100, sigmoid, Swish.
models.inputs: 1024 Hz, 1 s, peak-normalised (GAN); CNN data whitened with aLIGO design.
models.data: 1e5 signals in 5 classes (sine-Gaussian, ringdown, WNB, Gaussian pulse, IMRPhenomD BBH 30-70 Msun); CNN sets 2e5 at SNR 1-16.
models.training: GAN: BCE, Adam 2e-4 beta1 0.5, batch 512, 500 epochs. CNN: Adam 1e-3, batch 1000, 100 epochs.
models.results: CNN trained on generalised (simplex/uniform) GAN bursts is best overall at FAP 1e-3.
models.code: github.com/jmcginn/McGANn (from paper).
models.gaps: Generator channel typo, seeds.
models.adaptation_notes: The evaluation CNN on the five classes is S (Gaussian pulse is the only missing shape); the GAN generator needs a custom adversarial train step and a 'generated waveform' generator for the dataset.

models.title: GWSkyNet-Multi: A Machine Learning Multi-Class Classifier for LIGO-Virgo Public Alerts
models.authors: Thomas C. Abbott, Eitan Buffaz, Nicholas Vieira, Miriam Cabero, Daryl Haggard, Ashish Mahabal et al.
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full (text plus the confusion-matrix figure page rendered). Code and weights public on GitHub.
models.architecture: Three independent one-versus-all CNN classifiers (glitch-vs-all, NS-vs-all, BBH-vs-all) with one shared architecture (Fig 2). Two image branches (a 90x180x1 sky-map image and three 131x131x3 volume-projection images) each use stacked SeparableConv2D 3x3 layers (16, 16, then 32 filters in the volume branch) with 2x2 max pooling and global average pooling, then Dense layers; the scalar inputs (detector-network status, mean and max distance, log Bayes factors LogBSN and LogBCI, four image normalisation factors) go through small Dense layers; everything is concatenated into a Dense(1) output. The three scores are combined by a hierarchical rule (glitch first, then NS, then BBH; if no score exceeds its threshold, the class whose score is closest to threshold is chosen) because glitch-vs-all is the best performer. Grad-CAM is used for interpretability. It is a classifier of LIGO-Virgo Open Public Alert products (BAYESTAR skymaps), not of strain.
models.inputs: Not strain. Inputs derived from the BAYESTAR FITS sky map of an Open Public Alert: sky-map image, three volume-projected images, which detectors observed, mean and maximum distance estimates, log Bayes factors (signal vs noise, coherence vs incoherence) and normalisation factors. Prediction takes seconds after the alert.
models.data: 4267 events: 1267 glitches from O1/O2 (catalogued in Cabero et al. 2020 from noise-transient catalogues, plus 2-OGC candidates) and 3000 simulated events (1000 each of BBH, BNS, NSBH) from LALSuite waveforms injected in Gaussian noise coloured with the public O1, O2 and O3 PSDs. BH masses from the GWTC-2 'power law + peak' model (median posterior), NS masses uniform in [1,3] Msun, spins aligned (<=0.99 BH, <=0.05 NS). Split 81% train, 9% validation, 10% test (427). Applied to 40 O3a and 38 O3b public alerts (Tables 2 and 3).
models.training: Each one-versus-all model tuned by an hparams search (learning rate 1e-5 to 1e-1, batch size 5 to 110); selection prioritised accuracy with F1>=0.95. Thresholds set where FNR and FPR curves cross (glitch 32.3%, NS 62.2%, BBH 31.2%). Optimiser, loss, epochs and augmentation are not stated.
models.results: Test-set accuracy 95.1% (glitch), 94.4% (NS), 93.7% (BBH) one-versus-all; hierarchical multi-class accuracy 93.4%. On 40 O3a alerts it matches GWTC-2 on 36 (6 of 7 retracted); GWSkyNet-Multi 29/33 on non-retracted (see suspected errors: table implies 30/33), GWSkyNet 30/33, GraceDB 28/33. Four O3a misses: S190425z (a real BNS called glitch), S190630ag, S190816i, S190923y. 21 O3 events have more than one score above threshold and 4 have none.
models.code: https://github.com/GWML/GWSkyNet (MIT, 2021, includes .h5 weights for GWSkyNet and the one-vs-all models in nb/) and https://github.com/nayyer-raza/GWSkyNet-Multi (MIT, 2025, models/Multi-class_*.h5 ensemble weights).
models.gaps: No optimiser/loss/epoch details; training data are simulated skymaps and glitch OPAs, with detector-network (HL, HLV) composition not broken out; no FAR or ROC; BBH confusion matrix in Fig 7 duplicates the glitch panel; test set small (427) with no uncertainties.
models.adaptation_notes: GWSkyNet-Multi on BAYESTAR alert products.

models.title: Long Short-Term Memory for Early Warning Detection of Gravitational Waves
models.authors: Reem Alfaidi, Christopher Messenger
models.venue: arXiv preprint (gr-qc, 7 Feb 2024); no journal reference found in the PDF
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full, ROC figure page rendered.
models.architecture: Stacked four-layer LSTM (PyTorch), 32 hidden units per layer, input dimension 64 (64 whitened samples = 1/16 s are fed per step), final LSTM output to a Dense(16) layer then a 2-unit output; BCE-with-logits loss. It emits one prediction per 64 samples (16 Hz), i.e. a per-timestep signal-present score, and early warning is the first time the score crosses a threshold set from a false-alarm rate. Single detector, BBH only.
models.inputs: Whitened (then z-scored) simulated H1 strain at 1024 Hz, streamed in blocks of 64 samples; training windows 8 s, test series 12 s.
models.data: PyCBC SEOBNRv4_opt BBH, m1 power-law 5-95 Msun (m2 uniform 5 to m1), zero spin, random sky, polarisation and inclination, in Gaussian noise from the aLIGOZeroDetHighPower PSD (design sensitivity, single H1). Coalescence time uniform 4-9 s in an 8 s training window (so the merger can fall outside), 8-13 s in the 12 s test series; optimal SNR uniform 7-20 in training and 2-20 in test. 25% noise-only series. Training 1,000,000 series, validation 100,000, test 20,000. Per-step labels from cumulative optimal SNR (signal present when cumulative SNR>=5, reset after the merger).
models.training: 100 epochs (not converged), batch 1000, lr 1e-4, one NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GB), about 33 h; no stated optimiser. Best at 1e6 series (7e5 minimum to avoid over-fitting).
models.results: ROC (Fig 4) on 4 s maximised statistics shows the LSTM true-alarm probability about 2x lower than a single exact-template matched filter (an unrealistic upper bound) at FARs of 1/day, 1/6 h and 1/h; early warnings up to 4 s before merger at 1 false alarm per day; the LSTM's warning time is about half that of CSNR threshold 6 and two-thirds of CSNR threshold 8, comparable to threshold 10. Table 2 gives the shares of early warnings found by both, LSTM only and CSNR only.
models.code: No code link or data statement in the paper; GitHub keyword search found nothing (see code_repos).
models.gaps: Gaussian simulated noise only, single detector, BBH zero-spin only, no real data or glitches; test noise-only duration too short to resolve 1/day (ROC axis starts near 6e-5 Hz); no sky localisation; no timing or latency number; the paper has no DOI listed in the arXiv record.
models.adaptation_notes: Streaming LSTM with an exact-template matched-filter bound.

models.title: PyMerger: Detecting Binary Black Hole merger from Einstein Telescope Using Deep Learning
models.authors: Wathela Alhassan, T. Bulik, M. Suchenek
models.venue: arXiv preprint (astro-ph.IM, Oct 2023); later versions list the software paper Alhassan et al. 2024; no journal reference in this PDF
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full (text), code on GitHub; figures not rendered (the numbers needed are quoted in text/tables).
models.architecture: ResNet-101 image classifier (binary: injected BBH vs noise) on a 365x42x3 RGB 'image' built by stacking the STFT spectrograms of the three ET sub-detectors E1, E2, E3 as the three channels (TSDCD, three-sub-detector combined data); input layer adapted from the single-sub-detector (SSDD) model of Alhassan et al. 2022 (WTM1). Detection on continuous data by sliding a 5 s window over the three channels, cropping and stacking spectrograms, thresholding the class probability. PyMerger is the packaged tool (gwf input, 8192 or 4096 Hz).
models.inputs: 5 s STFT spectrograms (up to the cropped band) of E1, E2, E3 strain, normalised by the maximum intensity across the three; no whitening, no band-pass.
models.data: Simulated ET triangular 3x sub-detector Gaussian noise coloured by the ET-D PSD. 125,000 BBH injections (IMRPhenomD via LALSuite, masses 15-56 Msun and redshift 0.033-11 from the Belczynski et al. 2020 StarTrack population; uniform sky/inclination/polarisation/phase; Planck cosmology) split evenly over five lower cutoffs Flow (5, 10, 15, 20, 30 Hz) and five matched-filter SNR bins (4-5, 5-6, 6-7, 7-8, >8), plus 125,000 noise-only samples; 85,000/20,000/20,000 per class for train/test/validation. Continuous mock data: 3,610 injections (722 per SNR bin) at one per 5 s, 5 h 50 s per Flow per detector; and the ET-MDC1 mock data challenge (30.8 days, 1300 segments of 2048 s at 8192 Hz, 59,540 BNS, 6,578 BBH, 1,977 BHNS, Gaussian noise with no artifacts).
models.training: RMSprop, batch 256, lr 1e-4, 200 epochs (settings copied from WTM1). No glitches, no overlapping signals. Laptop inference: 1 h of 3-detector data in 1.9 min on a Core i7 MacBook Pro (4.7 min per hour for the single-sub-detector model).
models.results: Test-set detection accuracy at Flow 30 Hz rises from 60/60.5/84.5/94.5/98.5% (SSDD) to 78.5/84/99.5/100/100% (TSDCD) for SNR 4-5/5-6/6-7/7-8/>8; overall injected recall 0.818 and noise recall 0.994 on the 40,000 test set. On ET-MDC1 it recovers 5,566 of 6,578 BBH (84.6%), plus 11,477 of 59,540 BNS and 323 of 1,977 BHNS although trained on BBH only; one week of noise and null stream give 10 false detections at threshold 0.5, 1 at 0.3, 0 at 0.1 (null: 0).
models.code: https://github.com/wathela/PyMerger (exists; last push 2024; licence file not recognised (NOASSERTION); trained TFLite model included in the repo).
models.gaps: Gaussian noise only, no glitches; the 'FPR' curve in Sec 5 is really the missed fraction of injections; no ROC or FAR at a fixed efficiency for the injection test; detection threshold for MDC recovery counts not stated; SNR is matched-filter SNR per sub-detector.
models.adaptation_notes: ET triangle spectrogram ResNet; needs ET PSD and response.

models.title: Exploring gravitational-wave detection and parameter inference using Deep Learning methods
models.authors: João D. Álvares, José A. Font, Felipe F. Freitas, Osvaldo G. Freitas, António P. Morais, Solange Nunes et al.
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full, ROC figure page rendered.
models.architecture: Two image networks on constant-Q-transform spectrograms. Classifier: ResNet-101 (best of 18/34/50/101) with its head replaced by AdaptiveConcatPool2d, flatten, a batch-norm/dropout/linear/ReLU block and a 2-unit output (signal vs background), cross-entropy, input 275x275x3 (Table II) from 560x560 images; single-detector version (grey) and a three-detector version where H1, L1, V1 spectrograms are the R, G, B channels. Regression (PE): xResNet-18 with blur pooling and MC dropout, custom head with one linear output, MSE loss, 128x128x3 input (images 224x224 in Table I), one network per parameter (luminosity distance, network antenna power, chirp mass, effective inspiral spin chi_eff).
models.inputs: Spectrograms (constant-Q transform of a [-0.16, +0.4] s window around the merger) of strain from open O2 data, whitened by inverse spectrum truncation with the segment's own ASD, band-passed 20-300 Hz with 60/120/240 Hz notches; H1/L1/V1 mapped to RGB with detector time delays emulating the sky position.
models.data: Signals: pyCBC SEOBNRv4_ROM (classification) and SEOBNRv4HM_ROM, IMRPhenomPv2, IMRPhenomD (regression), plus-polarisation only, zero spin for classification, masses U(5,100) Msun, inclination pi/2, injected in O2 open data (single detector from one 500 s H1 segment starting GPS 1187058342 s, so heavy re-use of one noise stretch; three-detector case from coincident 500 s segments) in times not overlapping known events. Separate classification datasets at dL = 100, 300, 1000, 1500, 2000 Mpc (4000 train + 1000 validation signals each, with matching background), a mass-and-distance grid (1225 mass pairs x 20 distances) for scoring maps; regression sets of about 13-16k events each with dL U(100,4000) Mpc, inclination U(0,pi), aligned spin U(-1,1), SNR>5, plus a low-mass set (5-35 Msun, 15,538) merged for a 31,499 low-mass-weighted SEOBNRv4HM set (70/30 split). Applied to GWTC-1/-2 BBH events and 14 GWTC-1 marginal triggers.
models.training: Fastai-style one-cycle/cyclical LR, mixed precision, batch 8 images (classifier), LR 2e-3 with weight decay 1e-5 (max LR 10x), regression LR 1e-2 with wd 1e-3, batch 64; MC dropout (100 passes per event in calibration, 500 or 1500 on catalogue events) for uncertainties. Epoch counts not stated.
models.results: Classifier trained at 2000 Mpc: single detector accuracy 0.72 (PPV 0.80), three-detector RGB accuracy 0.82 with precision 0.9 (ROC AUC 0.87 in Fig 5, star at signal efficiency about 0.72 and background rejection about 0.91 for threshold 0.5), and trained-at-2000-Mpc networks score closer sources higher. All 10 GWTC-1 confident BBH events scored >=0.87; of 14 marginal O1/O2 triggers only MC151116 (0.73), MC161217 (0.72) and MC170705 (0.51) cross 0.5; 34 of 37 GWTC-2 BBH events score >0.5 (27 above 0.9, 31 above 0.7, 16 at 1.00). Regression: chirp-mass predictions within MC-dropout 3 sigma of the published 90% interval for 90% (33/37) of GWTC-2 events, six GWTC-1 events outside without the low-mass set, all but GW151226 inside with it; dL biased low on GWTC-2 (O2-noise training); regression RMSE 0.021 (normalised, Table II).
models.code: No code or data link in the paper; GitHub search found no repository for this work (see code_repos).
models.gaps: No separate test set or physical FAR (signal vs background spectrogram windows only); single-detector noise comes from one 500 s H1 segment; plus polarisation only and zero spin for detection; PE has no coverage/P-P statistics, only calibration histograms and 3-sigma overlap; Table II RMSE units unclear.
models.adaptation_notes: ResNet on HLV CQT images plus an MC-dropout regressor.

models.title: Search for binary black hole mergers in the third observing run of Advanced LIGO-Virgo using coherent WaveBurst enhanced with machine learning
models.authors: T. Mishra, B. O'Brien, M. Szczepanczyk, G. Vedovato, S. Bhaumik, V. Gayathri et al.
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full, Fig 3 page rendered.
models.architecture: Not a neural network: an XGBoost gradient-boosted decision-tree classifier (objective binary:logistic, hist tree method, lossguide growth, max depth 13, lr 0.03, min_child_weight 10, colsample 1.0, subsample and gamma chosen by a 9-point grid on AUC-PR, early stopping up to 20,000 trees) that takes 13 cWB summary statistics of each trigger (including S0/L for HL and S0/L, S1/L for HLV) and outputs a signal-vs-noise score W_XGB that is folded into the cWB detection statistic (reduced statistic eta_r); the ML replaces cWB's hard post-production vetoes. Two models (stellar-mass BBH and IMBH search configurations) for the HL network, plus a BBH model for HLV in a network study. Training and test run in minutes on one CPU. A separately trained XGBoost regressor (Ref. [24]) gives source-frame total mass.
models.inputs: Summary statistics of cWB (coherent WaveBurst) triggers, built from H1, L1 (and V1) O3 strain; not raw strain.
models.data: O3 open LIGO-Virgo strain. Background from time-shifted detector data (2000 yr of time-shifted background for training in each configuration; about 28,500 yr for testing the BBH/IMBH HL models per Table I; 550 yr training and 639 yr testing for the HLV study on 1/33 of O3). Simulations injected into data: (i) SEOBNRv4 aligned-spin stellar-mass BBH (total mass 5-100 Msun, q 1 to 1/4, uniform in comoving volume), 28,527 train and 20,077 test events (Table I values as printed), (ii) NR IMBH binaries (17 mass bins, 120-800 Msun, q 1 to 1/10), (iii) eccentric NR high-mass BBH (28 mass bins, 100-250 Msun, e 0.19-0.96; test only) and (iv) SEOBNRv4PHM precessing BBH (4-200 Msun, q to 1/20; test only). Standardised sample weights are used.
models.training: XGBoost with a standardised sample weight; early stopping on AUC-PR using a held-out part of the training data; trained separately for BBH and IMBH configurations over all of O3 (HL); detector-network study trains an HLV model on half of 1/33 of O3 (GPS 1241011102-1242485126).
models.results: All 15+10 (O3a+O3b) standard-cWB GWTC-3 BBH events recovered with equal or lower FAR; five further GWTC-3 events (GW190513, GW190707, GW190728, GW190929, GW191127) detected at FAR<1/yr that standard cWB vetoed; three extra cWB-only marginal candidates (190421_012633, 190904_174910 [likely seismic/60 Hz noise], 191223_151007). Detection efficiency at FAR<1/yr improved by 18% for both BBH and IMBH configurations (abstract: about 20%); sensitive hyper-volume (Power Law + Peak, FAR 2/yr) O3a 0.676 to 0.822 Gpc^3 yr and O3b 0.627 to 0.757; more sensitive to eccentric and precessing BBH outside the training set; HL network recovers about 7.7% more simulations than HLV at FAR<1/yr.
models.code: No code or data link in the paper; cWB is an LVK pipeline (cwb pipeline library 6.4.1) and no public XGBoost-enhanced cWB repository was found for this paper (see code_repos).
models.gaps: Efficiency is normalised by recovered (not total) injections in Fig 3; no ROC at fixed efficiency for a neural-net comparison; XGBoost is not a deep model; cWB trigger features not raw strain; only O3 HL; HLV test background short (about 640 yr).
models.adaptation_notes: XGBoost on cWB summary statistics; needs cWB runs on O3.

models.architecture: Two ensembles over 15 classical ML and 9 deep baselines. ShallowWaves: hard-voting of three tree models (Random Forest CART, Extremely Randomized Trees CART, XGBoost gbtree). models.title: Machine Learning based Glitch Veto for inspiral binary merger signals using Linear Chirp Transform
models.authors: N. Arutkeerthi, Xiyuan Li, Cindy Cui, SR Valluri
models.venue: arXiv preprint (2410.20269; downloaded PDF is v2, 27 Jul 2026, which cites 2025-2026 material; v1 was Oct 2024); no journal reference found
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full (text, Fig 6 confusion matrix described in text); code on GitHub.
models.architecture: Glitch-vs-merger classifier on 3D 'chirp-volume' spectrograms from a Linear Chirp Transform (LCT, an extra chirp-rate axis gamma from -30 to 30 in steps of 1). Each of the 61 chirp-rate slices (resized to 64x128) goes through a shared CNN (three blocks of two 3x3 convolutions with 32, 64, 128 filters, batch norm, ReLU, max-pool, dropout), adaptive average pooling to a 128-d vector, then a two-layer GRU across the 61 slices, layer norm, learnable attention pooling over slices, a Dense(64)+dropout head and a 2-way softmax. Focal loss, AdamW, cosine-annealing LR, mixed precision, gradient clipping, early stopping (57 epochs). Intended as a veto after the matched-filter stage. A PCA of histogram features is shown for visualisation only.
models.inputs: 6 s windows of H1/L1 strain, chirp transform over 30-500 Hz and 6000 samples at a 1 kHz Nyquist rate (array 61x471x6000, about 1.2 GB per signal) resized by linear interpolation to (61,64,128) (1.9 MB) and normalised per slice to [0,1].
models.data: Glitches: 708 time series from the PSO-matched-filter glitch set of Girgaonkar and Mohanty (loud transients that fooled a template search in 140 h of LIGO data, SNR 9 to 14401, H1 and L1), 6 s windows around the time of arrival with random shifts up to ±1 s. Mergers: 215 confirmed GWOSC events x 2 detectors = 430 real strain segments (SNR roughly 4-10), each time-shifted by up to ±1 s to double the set; 30 failed downloads dropped, leaving 830. 80/20 split: 1230 train, 308 validation.
models.training: NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti laptop GPU (4 GB); converged at 57 epochs by early stopping; best validation accuracy 95.45%; decision threshold tuned on the validation set to 0.44. Chirp transform plus resize takes 32.7 s per signal; classification takes 30 ms.
models.results: On the 308-sample validation set the model reaches about 96% accuracy at threshold 0.44 (95.45% best validation accuracy before threshold tuning), 13 errors (6 glitches and 7 mergers misclassified), macro precision/recall/F1 about 0.96 and class precision and recall 0.95-0.96. There is no separate test set and no FAR or ROC.
models.code: https://github.com/Arut123/Glitch-veto-GW-using-chirp (cited in the paper; exists; no licence; last push 2025; .h5/.hdf5 model files present).
models.gaps: Validation set doubles as the threshold-tuning set (no independent test); time-shifted copies of the same merger and both detectors of the same event can fall in both train and validation (leakage); class sources differ (matched-filter-selected loud glitches vs catalogued mergers, SNR 9-14401 vs 4-10) so features may reflect selection rather than morphology; not evaluated on real glitches that mimic mergers at low SNR or on a continuous background; no FAR numbers; not compared to chi-squared or other vetoes.

models.title: Enhancing gravitational-wave detection: a machine learning pipeline combination approach with robust uncertainty quantification
models.authors: Gregory Ashton, Ann-Kristin Malz, Nicolo Colombo
models.venue: Phys. Rev. D (DOI 10.1103/yfb3-fgf2); arXiv:2504.17587 (PDF is a later revision citing GWTC-4.0)
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read in full (Letter plus Supplemental Material), Fig 1 page rendered.
models.architecture: Post-search combination of CBC pipeline outputs: logistic regression (LR) and a one-hidden-layer MLP (100 ReLU neurons, scikit-learn, L-BFGS/Adam) take the per-pipeline feature vector (21 features per pipeline including IFAR, SNR, chi-squared, chirp mass, spin estimates; zeros where a pipeline has no candidate above IFAR 1 h; pastro deliberately excluded) from GstLAL, PyCBC, SPIIR, MBTA and cWB and output a signal/noise probability. Label-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction on a calibration split (non-conformity = 1 - LR probability) turns this into a calibrated 'conditional confidence: signal' per candidate. Not a strain-level model; ML operates on pipeline triggers.
models.inputs: Candidate lists (one maximum-SNR candidate per pipeline per 1 s cluster) uploaded by the LVK pipelines in a low-latency replay; for GWTC-3 application only IFAR, SNR and chirp mass are used (not for cWB) to keep exchangeability.
