models.title: Parameter estimation of microlensed gravitational waves with Conditional Variational Autoencoders
models.authors: Roberto Bada-Nerin, Oleg Bulashenko, Osvaldo Gramaxo Freitas, José A. Font
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF read (data, results, conclusions and appendix text); figures p-p/Fig 6-8 not rendered, values read from the text and Table I.
models.architecture: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE, following Gabbard et al. VItamin) with three networks (encoder, decoder, recognition) on whitened two-detector time series; 1D convolutional blocks (He init, no padding) followed by linear layers with LeakyReLU, latent space with KL term annealed during the first 100 epochs, loss = reconstruction + KL (converges near -2.5). It estimates only the two point-mass-lens parameters (relative source position y and characteristic lensing time t_M, the lens-mass proxy) and generates 8000 posterior samples per input. A second use feeds the CVAE 95% intervals (mean ± 2 sigma) as priors to bilby for a faster refinement.
models.inputs: 4 s of whitened (inverse spectrum truncation) H1 and L1 strain at 2048 Hz, signal injected at a random time in an 8 s segment.
models.data: Simulated microlensed and unlensed BBH waveforms from bilby with IMRPhenomXPHM, component masses U(35,80) Msun, default bilby priors otherwise, lensing parameters y in [0.01,3.0] and t_M in [0.001,0.2] s (lens masses about 50-104 Msun in the redshifted frame), SNR in [8,40], Gaussian noise coloured by O3a PSDs (Dataset 3 of Gramaxo Freitas et al.). Lensing applied as an amplification factor F(f; t_M, y) to the unlensed frequency-domain waveform. Sizes: 1,000,000 train, 20,000 validation and 1,000 test, non-overlapping.
models.training: 1,078 epochs to best validation loss; lr annealed then fixed at 1e-5 after epoch 100; 7-8 hours of training; no overfitting (train and validation loss close). Inference: about 4 s per waveform for the CVAE vs about 54,000 s for bilby.
models.results: p-p plot close to the diagonal for y and t_M; about 95% of true values inside the 95% intervals at all SNRs (error accumulation at high y and t_M not explained); posterior widths grow at low SNR but stay much narrower than the prior; CVAE is about four orders of magnitude faster than bilby (average 4 s vs 54,045 s over 17 waveforms; up to five orders in Table III); CVAE-informed bilby priors cut the average bilby runtime by 47.9% without degrading accuracy (KS statistics between runs comparable, except waveform 9).
models.code: No code link or data availability statement in the paper; GitHub search reported in code_repos.
models.gaps: Simulated Gaussian-noise data only, no real events or glitches; only two lensing parameters with all other source parameters fixed to truth in the bilby comparison; point-mass lens only; the 17-waveform timing comparison is small; no ROC/detection, no lensed-vs-unlensed classification; waveforms 4, 16, 18, 19 failed to converge in uninformed bilby runs.
models.adaptation_notes: CVAE for microlensing parameters.

models.title: Rapid detection of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers using sparse dictionary learning
models.authors: Charles Badger, Rahul Srinivasan, Alejandro Torres-Forne, Marie Anne Bizouard, Jose A. Font, Mairi Sakellariadou, Astrid Lamberts
models.venue: arXiv preprint (v3, 21 Mar 2025); no journal reference on the arXiv record
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF read in full, text plus Figs 3-8 viewed as images).
models.architecture: Not a neural network: sparse dictionary learning (SDL). A dictionary D (patch length w=512, p=768 patches = 1.5w, L1 regularisation lambda=1e-4, LASSO / basis-pursuit) is learned from 150 whitened noise-free IMRPhenomD BBH waveforms aligned at merger; a 0.375 s data window s is reconstructed as h_r = D alpha_min by minimising ||s-h||^2 + lambda||alpha||_1. Detection statistic = normalised overlap O(s,h_r) between data and reconstruction (a matched-SNR statistic of the reconstruction was tried and was worse). Detection threshold set from a noise-only overlap distribution.
models.inputs: Single-detector (H1) whitened strain in 0.375 s windows at 8192 Hz (3072 samples); whitened with the detector PSD; no multi-detector coincidence.
models.data: Training: 100/150/200 zero-spin IMRPhenomD BBH waveforms (primary 3-60 Msun, q near 1, redshift 0-8, uniform sky/phase), 513 dictionaries scanned over w, p, lambda using 25 validation + 25 test signals. Test: (a) 150,000 flat-prior BBHs (Mtot 5-80 Msun, z 0-8, q 1-5) and an astrophysical one-year population (catalogue of ref 23, default model, COSMIC v3.4.0, 5-45 Msun, metallicity 1-100% solar) injected in simulated A+ Hanford noise; (b) real O3b Hanford data around the 35 GWTC-3 O3b events with p_astro>0.5 (Gravity Spy catalogue used to remove glitches from the noise-only FAR sample). Matched-filter comparison: single-detector bank of 4582 templates, 97% minimal match, 3.5PN non-spinning.
models.training: Dictionary learning via LASSO alternating minimisation; each dictionary takes 5 to 454 s on an Intel E5-2698 v4 CPU (time grows with patch length). Hyperparameters chosen by hand to maximise validation overlap. No GPU, no epochs/batch size (not a gradient-trained network).
models.results: Overlap-statistic TPR over the full astrophysical population is only about 6% at FAR 12/yr (Fig 4, read from figure) versus about 22% for the single-detector matched filter on the same injections; at fixed injected SNR rho_opt>=15 injections exceed the FAR=12/yr overlap threshold (O>=0.35); SDL/MF 'universe volume' ratio <SNR^3> is 0.81 (astro) and 0.66 (flat). Six of 35 O3b events have O>=0.5 and FAR<=12/yr after glitch removal. Reconstruction of all 35 events takes 24.6 s (0.7 s per event) on an AMD EPYC 7502.
models.code: https://github.com/Rahul-Srinivasan/GW_DictionaryLearning (exists; no licence file; last push 2025-03-11; repository holds README and MATLAB_Dictionary_Code.zip (6 KB); no trained dictionary/weights file found by tree listing). Paper says code 'will be made available'.
models.gaps: Single detector only; zero spins; Gaussian simulated A+ noise for all FAR claims below 12/yr (extrapolated); no glitch handling inside the method (Gravity Spy glitches were removed from the noise sample by hand); real-data FAR floor 12/yr from one month; no timing comparison with matched filter (authors state this is open); no multi-detector coincidence.
models.adaptation_notes: Single-detector denoising autoencoder with an overlap statistic; A+ Gaussian noise.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Detection: compare via TPR/efficiency at a stated FAR (per year) or sensitive distance/volume at FAR (MLGWSC-1 style). Papers reporting accuracy/AUC on balanced sets or FAP per segment are not directly comparable. Here the only FAR values supported by data are >=12/yr (1 month of Gaussian noise); the quoted FAR=1e-3/yr TPRs are extrapolated. Single detector, flat 0.375 s windows; not comparable to MLGWSC-1 network FAR curves. Non-neural method.
suspected_errors_extracted: Fig 7 contours versus text: Sec III A / Sec IV claim TPR>=0.9 at FAR=12/yr for rho_opt>=12.5, but the log10 TPR=-0.01 (TPR 0.98) iso-line sits at rho_opt~15-17 and the -0.5 (0.32) line at ~10.5-11, so interpolation gives roughly 0.5-0.6 at rho_opt=12.5 (reading uncertainty +-1 in rho_opt).

Fig 4 flat-prior overlap TPR at FAR=1e-3/yr is about 0.03 (read from figure) while the text quotes 1-2% for overlap at that FAR; also all FAR<12/yr points are extrapolated from 1 month of data (stated by authors).

Overlap threshold for FAR=12/yr is ~0.33-0.35 in simulated A+ noise (Fig 5) but ~0.49 in real glitch-free O3b noise (Fig 8), so the 'rho_opt>=15 is confidently detected' statement is not transferable to real data; 6/35 real events recovered.

The explanation that normalised overlap 'compares only phases' while matched SNR includes amplitude is imprecise: the normalised overlap is amplitude-independent but not phase-only; not a numerical error.

models.title: Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction using Deep Neural Networks for Clustering of LIGO Data
models.authors: Sara Bahaadini, Yunan Wu, Scott Coughlin, Michael Zevin, Aggelos K. Katsaggelos
models.venue: arXiv preprint (formatted for IEEE Trans. Neural Networks and Learning Systems; no journal reference on the arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv (all 7 pages read; Fig 6 viewed as image).
models.architecture: Siamese convolutional embedding network (pairs of Gravity Spy spectrogram images, shared weights Theta) trained with a cosine-distance contrastive loss on labelled positive/negative pairs plus an unsupervised regulariser on all pairs. Two variants: (i) auto-encoder based (decoders H1, H2 reconstruct the inputs; weight alpha trades off J_D and J_G, L2 regularisation beta) and (ii) VAT based (virtual adversarial training: KL divergence between outputs for x and x+r_vadv, power-iteration approximation of r_vadv). Embedding then clustered with a clustering algorithm (k-means named in the auto-encoder section). Conv / max-pool / fully-connected layer sizes are not given.
models.inputs: Gravity Spy Omega-scan spectrogram images of glitches (single 'Omega scan' images per Fig 5; image size, durations and channels not stated); pairs labelled positive (same class), negative (different classes) or unknown.
models.data: Gravity Spy training set v1.2 (7932 glitches, 22 classes, Hanford+Livingston, Table I; improved over v1.0 by removing incorrect samples). Transfer-style protocol: the first 10 classes train the network, the remaining 10 classes (disjoint) are clustered; the paper states 'first 10' and 'remaining 10' although 22 classes are listed (2 classes unaccounted). Evaluation: NMI of the clustering and accuracy of pair classification (same vs different class).
models.training: Not given: optimiser, learning rate, epochs, batch size, alpha, beta, epsilon, k for k-means, and seeds are all unstated. Labelled-data fraction varied (0.1, 1, 30, 50, 85 %) in Fig 6 and Table II.
models.results: NMI: raw features 0.43, PCA 0.43, DIRECT (supervised baseline) 0.53, auto-encoder+discriminative 0.55, VAT+discriminative 0.61 (Table III). Fig 6: VAT-based proposed model NMI rises 0.49 -> 0.66 and DIRECT 0.36 -> 0.59 as labelled data goes 0.1 -> 85 %. Pair-classification accuracy 49.07% (0.1% labels and 1% labels) rising to 82.62% (85% labels).
models.code: No code link in the paper; GitHub keyword search (title, authors, Gravity Spy DIRECT) found no repository. Dataset: Gravity Spy v1.2 on Zenodo (doi 10.5281/zenodo.1476156, cited as ref 17).
models.gaps: No architecture sizes, hyperparameters, clustering algorithm settings or seeds; single train/cluster class split with no repeats or error bars; which labelled fraction Table III corresponds to is not stated; which 10 classes are used is not named; no per-class results; no computational cost.

models.title: Deep learning for clustering of continuous gravitational wave candidates
models.authors: Banafsheh Beheshtipour, Maria Alessandra Papa
models.access: Open arXiv (all 9 pages read; Figs 6-7 viewed as images).
models.architecture: Mask R-CNN instance-segmentation network (Matterport Keras implementation, ref 45) with ResNet-101 + Feature Pyramid Network backbone; SGD optimiser; a region is accepted as a 'signal cluster' when its score is >=0.5; ground-truth masks reduced internally to 28x28 floats.
models.inputs: 256x256-pixel sub-images of the (f, fdot) plane of Einstein@Home all-sky search results (ref 40) for each 50 mHz band: a 60000x22000-pixel image coloured by the detection statistic (beta_S/GLtLr, also 2F), max over sky per pixel, averaged over 40x40-pixel blocks (a factor >1500 smaller); empty pixels remain.
models.data: Einstein@Home search results with fake signals added; training set 700 sub-images, test set 670 sub-images; ground-truth cluster masks drawn by hand (Pixelmator on a tablet, ~1 min per cluster) for loud, by-eye visible signals only; the test set holds 1171 signal clusters. Augmentation: flips, random rescaling of pixel values (0.1-1.5) and 20% pixel dropout.
models.training: Start from pre-trained Mask R-CNN weights; 3 stages: head layers 100 epochs, first three levels 300 epochs, full network 1000 epochs; learning rate 0.001 (stages 1-2) and 0.0001 (stage 3); batch size 15, weight decay 1e-5, momentum 0.9; Quadro GV100 32 GB; the text says the run 'took about 28 hours' (sentence ambiguous, probably training).
models.results: Test-set efficiency 97% (1137 of 1171 signal clusters found; network returned 1345 clusters). Efficiency above 95% for beta_S/GLtLr>17 (2F>18), 100% above 35 (2F>40). 90% of cluster maxima lie within ~1e-4 Hz and ~1e-11 Hz/s of the true signal. For a ~90 Hz population with h0~1.75e-25 the overall efficiency is ~67%; the same network retrained on much fainter signals reaches only ~17% at beta~20 and ~13% for beta<=15.
models.code: No code link or repository for the authors' network (GitHub keyword searches found none); built on the Matterport Mask_RCNN repository (exists; licence NOASSERTION; last push 2024).
models.gaps: Only loud, by-eye-identifiable signals; 2D projection of a 4D problem; low-resolution images; no false-alarm rate on noise-only data; the training cluster count is garbled by a page break in the extracted text ('124' / '45', probably 1245; not verified visually); no table comparing with the deterministic clustering.

models.title: Deep learning for clustering of continuous gravitational wave candidates II: identification of low-SNR candidates
models.authors: Banafsheh Beheshtipour, Maria Alessandra Papa
models.access: Open arXiv (all 9 pages read; Figs 5-10 viewed as images).
models.architecture: Same Mask R-CNN (ResNet-101 + FPN) as paper I, used as a second 'weak-signal' network (WeakSigN) on higher-resolution 512x512 sub-images (12x12-pixel averaging for O2 versus 40x40 in paper I); initialised from the paper-I weights; combined with the paper-I 'loud-signal' network (LoudSigN) in a cascade: LoudSigN clusters are set to empty, then WeakSigN runs on the remainder. Score threshold 0.5.
models.inputs: (f, fdot) images of Einstein@Home O2 all-sky results (20-600 Hz, fdot -2.6e-9 to 2.6e-10 Hz/s; 64 coherent searches of 60 h each, H1+L1), 512x512-pixel slices of 1.7 mHz x 1.7e-10 Hz/s; detection statistic = odds ratio beta_S/GLtLr; >99% of pixels empty (filled with the image minimum).
models.data: Fake weak signals added to O2 data (uniform sky, cos inclination, polarisation; f in 20-600 Hz); 515 training, 218 validation, 347 test sub-images (one weak cluster each, hand-marked ground truth, ~4 min per signal); cascade evaluated on 1684 fake signals at 40-579 Hz; false alarms on 1774 randomly chosen 50 mHz bands of the real O2 result set.
models.training: Three stages as in paper I but shorter: 60, 120 and 1000 epochs; learning rate 0.001, weight decay 1e-5, momentum 0.9; batch size 2 (paper I: 15); about 40 hours on a 32 GB GPU. Appendix B: efficiency 71% / 78% / 80% for 128 / 257 / 515 training images.
models.results: WeakSigN alone: 80% (276/347, +-2%) on weak-signal test images. Cascade: all signals detected at normalised amplitude >=1/40 sqrt(Hz), >95% down to ~1/54, 92% above 1/60 (deterministic clustering of the O2 search: 83%); at ~1/80 the text says 80% versus <50% for deterministic clustering (Fig 9 lowest bin shows ~0.84 versus ~0.57). False alarms about half those of the deterministic method, with peaks up to four times larger at 250-350 Hz. Frequency / spin-down uncertainty 1.68x / 1.25x smaller than the deterministic clustering.
models.code: No code or repository found (no code statement in the paper; GitHub keyword searches found none); built on Matterport Mask_RCNN. Sky-position uncertainty of WeakSigN is much worse than deterministic clustering (stated).
models.gaps: Only (f, fdot) clustering, no sky clustering (4D problem); false-alarm numbers given only as plotted histograms and an 'about half' statement; training-set coverage poor at 250-350 Hz; no uncertainty on cascade efficiencies; no code.
models.adaptation_notes: Cascade clustering of Einstein@Home O2 candidates.

models.title: GraviBERT: Transformer-based inference for gravitational-wave time series
models.authors: Martin Benedikt, Ippocratis D. Saltas
models.venue: arXiv preprint (no journal reference on the arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF text read in full, 31 pages including tables; figures A1, 6-8 inspected through captions/axis text only).
models.architecture: Hybrid CNN + Transformer regressor. Feature extractor: InceptionTime-style, stem conv k=7 -> 64 channels, 3 main blocks each of 3 Inception modules (bottleneck k=1 to 32 channels; parallel convs k=10/20/40 with 32/48/64 filters per branch; max-pool branch) with residual connection and a stride-2 max-pool per block (total x8 downsampling, ~2 ms token), single BatchNorm after concatenation. Linear projection to d_model 256, learnable [CLS] token, sinusoidal positions, 4-layer / 4-head Transformer encoder (d_ff 512, GELU, dropout 0.10); [CLS] output to an MLP head (256, 64, linear 4). Predicts (m1, m2, chi_eff, effective distance d) as point estimates; uncertainty by MC dropout (100 passes). Self-supervised BERT-style pretraining: contiguous spans (mean length 32, ratio 0.15, alternating masked/unmasked segments) zeroed and a latent target from the unmasked input reconstructed with MSE.
models.inputs: Single-channel time series, 4096 samples at 4096 Hz (1 s), waveform plus coloured Gaussian noise; scaled by 1e21; padded to length; targets min-max scaled to [0,1].
models.data: Simulated only: SEOBNRv4 (PyCBC) BBH on a regular grid over m1,m2 in [5,150] Msun, spins in [-0.4,0.4] (aligned), effective distance rescaled to enforce a fixed network SNR of 10 or 30; flow=20 Hz; ET-B PSD noise (ET design normally 5 Hz); no extrinsic parameters, no antenna pattern. Datasets ~20k / ~50k / ~80k training samples, 80/10/10 split (10,000 test). Domain adaptation: second noise domain called 'LVK' (PSD not named) with 5,000 or 10,000 fine-tuning samples; waveform adaptation: IMRPhenomD at 5,000 / 10,000 samples.
models.training: Pretraining: AdamW lr 1e-4, cosine with 10% warm-up, batch 250, up to 200 epochs (best checkpoint epoch 24 by validation loss, Fig A1a). Fine-tune / scratch: AdamW lr 5e-4, weight decay 1e-2, batch 250, up to 120 epochs, grad clip 1.0, MSE loss. Single NVIDIA A100. Compute: scratch 80-350 min, pretrained 13-170 min to the same validation loss (Table 1). No hyperparameter search.
models.results: In-domain (ET noise): pretraining reduces MAE by up to 31% (large dataset, SNR 30) and speeds convergence up to 6.6x; R^2>=0.90 for all parameters; large dataset SNR 10 MAE m1 5.44, m2 4.51 Msun, chi_eff 0.03, d 5043 (effective Mpc). Domain adaptation ET->'LVK' noise: MAE reduction 9-47%, up to 15x faster. Cross-waveform SEOBNRv4->IMRPhenomD: zero-shot R^2 0.65 (chi_eff) to 0.97, fine-tuning gains 19-44% in MAE and 6-15x speed. Latency 10.6+-0.5 ms (batch 1), 1895 samples/s at batch 250.
models.code: GitHub https://github.com/GraviBERT/GraviBERT (exists; MIT; last push 2026-02-23; 4 checkpoint .pth files of ~14.1 MB: SNR10/SNR30 large_pretrained and 10000_LIGO_finetuned). Zenodo record 18671949 (CC-BY-4.0, GraviBERT-main.zip 61 MB, 2026-02-17) cited in the paper as code and pretrained models.
models.gaps: Simulated Gaussian noise only (no real data, no glitches); point estimates with MC dropout, not posteriors; no coverage / p-p test of the MC-dropout sigma; the 'LVK' PSD is not named; only 4 intrinsic parameters at fixed SNR 10/30 with a grid prior; test grid shares the training grid (off-grid generalisation untested, stated); single seed, no error bars on MAE/R^2; no hyperparameter search; effective distance is not a physical distance.
models.adaptation_notes: GraviBERT transformer regression on ET noise.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Posterior quality (p-p, KL/JS divergence, ESS, runtime); not comparable to detection or classification metrics. Here only point-estimate MAE/R^2 on a grid, fixed SNR, simulated ET-B noise, 4 parameters: not comparable to DINGO-style posterior metrics. 'Distance' is a rescaling factor, not astrophysical.
suspected_errors_extracted: Abstract/conclusion say MAE in effective spin reaches ~1e-3 at SNR 10, but Table 2 gives chi_eff MAE 0.03 (large dataset, pretrained, SNR 10). The 3.8e-3 in Sec 5.2 is the mean of signed errors averaged within grid-point groups (a bias), not an MAE; the abstract figure is therefore about 8x too optimistic as an MAE.

Sec 5.2 quotes 'mean relative precision' of the masses as 3-6% (SNR 10) from signed group means, while Table 2 MAE for m1 is 5.44 Msun (about 9% for a typical 60 Msun); sign cancellation understates the typical error.

MC-dropout 1 sigma for d is 2000-4000 Mpc at SNR 10 whereas the MAE is ~5000 Mpc, and for masses 2-4 Msun vs MAE 4.5-5.4 Msun: the stated sigma is smaller than the actual error by roughly 1.5-2x, so it is not calibrated (no coverage test given).

Sec 5.4: 'maximum throughput 1895 events/s (0.48 ms per waveform at batch 250, including MC Dropout)'. 250/0.1320 s = 1894 samples/s, i.e. 0.528 ms per waveform; 0.48 ms is 119.4 ms/250 (the standard pass). Also the figure counts one stochastic pass, not the 100 passes used for the reported metrics (which would be about 19 samples/s). Table 9 batch-1 throughput 96.3/s versus text 94/s (10.6 ms -> 94.3/s).
Sec 5.3 says mass and distance improve 13-27% under domain adaptation, but Table 4 lists d at 10,000 samples SNR 10 as 9% (and 13% is the minimum for m2).

Abstract: 'R^2 consistently exceeding 0.9 for mass parameters at SNR=10 compared to 0.74-0.87 when training from scratch' refers to the cross-waveform fine-tuning case (Sec 5.3), not in-domain results, where scratch R^2 is already 0.90-0.95.

models.title: Searching for binary black hole mergers with deep learning in Advanced LIGO's third observing run
models.authors: Damon Beveridge, Alistair McLeod, Linqing Wen, Weichangfeng Guo, Andreas Wicenec
models.venue: arXiv preprint v2 (Jul 2026); DOI 10.1103/3yph-35r4 given on the arXiv record (journal not stated in the text)
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF text read in full, 23 pages; Fig 7 viewed as image).
models.architecture: Hybrid pipeline: matched filtering (97,802-template subset of the GstLAL O2 bank, both masses >2 Msun, SEOBNRv4_ROM, flow 15 Hz, data at 2048 Hz, weekly PSDs) -> per-second peak-finding on SNR time series (SNR>4 in at least one detector, coincident peak within ~10 ms in the other) -> keep the 10 highest-network-SNR templates per second -> a TensorFlow CNN/ResNet/fully-connected model (architecture of prior work, ref 57) takes the 1 s H1+L1 SNR time series and outputs an unbounded score (sigmoid removed after training; exported to ONNX, CPU inference) -> 16 stepwise predictions per trigger averaged, max over the 10 templates = ranking statistic -> FAR from 100 time-shifted backgrounds (~1.5 yr per week of data, exponential tail fit) -> p_astro by an FGMC / GWCelery-style Bayes factor (tuned rho_th 8.5/7.25, F_th 1e-4).
models.inputs: Matched-filter SNR time series (H1 and L1, 1 s windows at 2048 Hz) for 10 templates per second; not strain.
models.data: Training: first week of O3 H1/L1 data as noise (time-offset between detectors so no coincidence), 100,000 noise-only plus 100,000 injected-BBH one-second samples, 30% of samples with Omicron glitches (SNR>6) aligned in frequency with injections, 20% validation; injections SEOBNRv4PHM/v4P, component masses 2-100 Msun, linearly decreasing chirp-mass density (2:1), network SNR power law -3 over 6-1000. Evaluation: 83,815 BBH injections (LVK GWTC-3 injection set) in alternate weeks of O3, plus the offline search of the full O3 (106.2 d O3a, 96.0 d O3b of coincident data; 104.6 d and 94.7 d after cuts), Virgo unused.
models.training: Not stated in this paper (optimiser, epochs, learning rate, batch size all refer to ref 57); 32-bit floats; CPU inference via ONNX Runtime 1.17.
models.results: Sensitivity (p_astro>=0.5, FAR<2/day): comparable to all-source pipelines above source-frame chirp mass ~25 Msun, below which (network SNR<~15) it falls; overall 23,238 of 83,815 injections detected (27.7%) vs 31,392 for PyCBC-BBH and 29,303 for GstLAL; 2,612 unique detections (most of any pipeline); combined VT increases when added. Offline O3 search: 33 candidates (23 in O3a, 10 in O3b): 31 in GWTC, GW190605_025957 (IAS-HOM) and one new, GW190929_091722 (p_astro 0.63, FAR 27/yr, SNR 6.7, total mass 171 +172/-58 Msun).
models.code: https://github.com/damonbeveridge/new_BBH_O3_candidate-UWA (exists; no licence; last push 2025-12-05): only parameter-estimation configs and posterior_samples.h5 (27 MB) for the new candidate, no search pipeline code and no trained model weights. Author's other public repo 'gravflows' (2022) is an unrelated normalising-flow project. The search code is not public.
models.gaps: Training hyperparameters; template-bank limited to >2 Msun both masses and masses <=100 Msun; no single-detector or Virgo search; four candidates missed due to glitch-dominated long templates; no data-quality failure vetoes beyond Omicron at the new candidate; p_astro tuned on injections of the same type used for sensitivity (minimum network SNR 6) so pastro of low-SNR candidates is uncertain; the new candidate lies partly outside the trained mass range.
models.adaptation_notes: CNN on matched-filter SNR series over a full O3 search; LVK injection campaign.

models.authors: Jericho Cain
models.access: Open arXiv (v7; all 15 pages read in text; Fig 5 not inspected as image, values taken from caption and text).
models.architecture: Unsupervised LSTM autoencoder on CWT scalograms: bidirectional LSTM encoder (64 hidden units) -> fully connected layer to a 32-d latent -> mirrored bidirectional LSTM decoder (64 units) -> fully connected output reconstructing the 8 x 4096 scalogram; MSE loss; anomaly score = L2 reconstruction error with a threshold (0.667 in normalised units).
models.inputs: H1 strain 32 s segments at 4096 Hz: 15 Hz high-pass, 1024 Hz low-pass, whitening, 4x decimation to 1024 Hz (32,768 samples), Morlet CWT (omega0=6) with 8 scales over 20-512 Hz, log(1+|W|^2), per-scale z-scoring with training statistics, local averaging to 4096 time bins (about 7.8 ms) -> 8 x 4096.
models.data: Real LIGO Hanford O4 (GWTC-4.0, 2023-24) from GWOSC: 1991 noise segments from science mode (+-16 s from catalogue events excluded) split 80/20 (1592 train / 399 test) plus 102 confirmed events (of 126 GWTC-4.0 events; 24 dropped for data quality, unconfirmed status or H1 off) all reserved for the test set (501 test samples: 102 signals, 399 noise). Training uses noise only. Synthetic validation: post-Newtonian-style chirps (m 10-80 Msun, D 100-1000 Mpc, SNR 8-25) in coloured Gaussian noise from an analytic aLIGO design PSD. Earlier multi-run O1-O4 variant: 207 events plus the 1991 noise segments.
models.training: SGD, lr 0.001, momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-5, early stopping on validation-loss plateau (validation set composition not stated); batch size and epochs not stated; threshold chosen on precision-recall analysis (Sec 3) or F1 maximisation (Sec 4.4). CPU benchmark AMD Ryzen 9 9950X: 161.5+-1.0 ms CWT + 2.9+-0.2 ms inference per 32 s segment.
models.results: O4 H1: precision 97.0%, recall 96.1%, F1 96.6%, specificity ~99.2%, ROC-AUC 0.994, AP 0.967 on 102 signals + 399 noise segments (98 TP, 4 FN, 396 TN, 3 FP); reconstruction error noise 0.484+-0.095, signals 0.774+-0.152. Multi-run (O1-O4) training gave precision 96% and recall 52% with run-clustered errors (Spearman 0.68); synthetic data gave precision 92.3%, recall 67.6%, AUC 0.806.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Anomaly detection: AUC/FPR against a chosen anomaly set; definitions of normal and anomalous differ. Here the 'signals' are 102 confirmed O4 events and the 'noise' is 399 random science-mode segments, i.e. event-vs-random-segment discrimination at fixed 20% signal prevalence, with no FAR in events/yr: not comparable to MLGWSC-1 style sensitivity.
suspected_errors_extracted: Possible non-astrophysical separation: the paper's own Sec 6.1 shows the model's earlier skill 'relied on subtle run-specific whitening signatures' (AUC 0.78 -> 0.44 after uniform re-whitening) rather than intrinsic signal/noise differences. The final AUC 0.994 uses event-centred windows versus randomly placed windows from the same run with no control for such differences, so the number may partly reflect data-selection/conditioning effects (caution; not proven).

Threshold selection is described two ways: Sec 3 says optimised on validation data to maximise recall at precision >90%; Sec 4.4 says it maximises F1 giving 0.667. All signals are reserved for the test set, so no signal-containing validation set exists, hence the F1-optimal threshold was evidently set on the test set (leaks into the reported precision/recall).
Event counts do not agree: Sec 4.2 has 126 O4 plus 90 O1-O3 (216) events while Sec 6.1 says 207 events for O1-O4; with 102 usable O4 events the O1-O4 total would be 192.
Scale range: CWT limited to 8 scales over 20-512 Hz, yet the description of Fig 1 claims a chirp band from ~100 to 800 Hz (above Nyquist of the 1024 Hz data).
Specificity quoted as 99.2% in the abstract text but 0.993 in the CI sentence (396/399 = 0.9925); precision CI upper bound 0.993 differs slightly from a Wilson calculation (~0.990).

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Space-based (LISA/Taiji/TianQin) synthetic data; not comparable to ground-based FAR metrics. Task is mass-ratio classification of noiseless simulated signals, not detection; no ground-based relevance beyond a recurrent-network baseline.
suspected_errors_extracted: Text misreports the confusion matrices: 'classes A and D, 99.6% training / 93% testing from class B and 85.3% / 89.2% from class C'. In Figs 28-29 these percentages are column (precision) values; the recall for B is 82.9% (train) / 88.7% (test) and for C 99.6% / 93.3%. Class B training recall 82.9% (231 of 1350 B sent to C) is therefore the weak point, not C.

'Overall accuracy 95.5741%' does not match the confusion matrices: training 5164/5400 = 95.63%, test 573/600 = 95.5%; the 4-digit figure is presumably from MATLAB's progress window and is unclear which split it covers.

Data leakage in the 4-class evaluation: classes A and D are enlarged by cloning (repmat) before the random 90/10 split, and files are cut into 32,000-point segments before splitting, so identical or neighbouring segments appear in both training and test sets; the 100% accuracy for A and D is therefore not independent evidence.
Class confound: only class D contains added noise, and time step and duration differ by class (0.3333-0.01 s, 4-16 min), so the network can separate D by noise or sampling rather than by mass ratio.
Counts do not reconcile: text says 4067 segments (7%/44%/40%/7% for A/B/C/D) but the matrices total 6000 balanced segments (1500 per class); no explanation of the undersampling of B/C.

2-class matrices use label 'S' where the text defines class 'L' (H/L); classes and mass ratios (q up to 950 with one mass fixed at 1e3 Msun) imply massive-binary LISA sources, so the title 'Characterization of GW signals' overstates the task.
The 2-class headline 100% accuracy is on 20 test samples.

models.title: Finding the origin of noise transients in LIGO data with machine learning
models.authors: Marco Cavaglia, Kai Staats, Teerth Gill
models.access: Open arXiv 1812.05225 (full text read; figures not rendered). Published Commun. Comput. Phys. 25 (2019).
models.architecture: Not a neural network: random forest (scikit-learn, 500 estimators, iterative feature-importance threshold 0.005 for the magnetometer set, 0 for the air-compressor set) and genetic programming (Karoo GP tree-based GP: base/max tree depth 10 (5 in the size study), min depth 3, population 300, 100-150 generations, tournament size 10-20). The task is binary glitch-vs-background classification used to rank auxiliary channels by importance, to find the instrumental origin of a glitch class.
models.inputs: Omicron trigger features from auxiliary channels (SNR, etc.; 4494 features from 749 channels for the magnetometer set; 2856 features from 429 channels for the air-compressor set). Highest-SNR Omicron trigger within +-0.1 s of each glitch time.
models.data: Two glitch sets from real Advanced LIGO data: 2049 hveto-identified glitches in a Livingston EX magnetometer/mains monitor (Feb-Apr 2017, O2; 2000 triggers used) and 16 Hanford air-compressor glitches at ~50 Hz (O1, Dec 2015). Background label-0 triggers: strain-channel Omicron triggers with SNR>6 outside +-10 s of any glitch. 2/3 train+validation, 1/3 test.

models.architecture: GSpyNetTreeS: YOLO-style (YOLOv3-like) object detector on a Q-transform image. Simplified Darknet backbone with 24 Darknet convolutional layers (outputs taken from layers 15 and 24), a second component of a few Darknet conv layers plus upsampling and concatenation, two output grids at different scales for regions of different size; six anchor boxes from K-means (centroids of the training bounding boxes). models.inputs: 1-second Q-transform time-frequency images (whitened strain; image rendering with normalised pixel energy). Regions of excess power defined as clusters of >=28 connected loud pixels, loud = normalised energy >=10.5 (98th percentile of pixels).
models.data: GSpyNetTree data set (Alvarez-Lopez et al. 2024): Gravity Spy glitches (Blip, Low frequency blip, Low frequency line, Scattering, Scratchy) from O3 H1/L1 plus simulated BBH injections (IMRPhenomPv2, total mass 5-350 Msun, component masses 2-175, SNR 8-35, spins 0.05-0.95) in 64 s quiet segments. 13,000 unique images, augmented by random time shifts of up to 0.25 s to 23,749 images; split ~80/10/10: train 19,236 / validation 2,138 / test 2,375 images. Region counts: GW 11,479/1,249/1,385; Blip 3,993/464/513; Low-freq blip 3,440/374/449; Low-freq line 5,767/651/667; Scattering 1,832/198/250; Scratchy 19,382/2,124/2,419 (train/val/test). models.title: Identification and characterization of distorted gravitational waves by lensing using deep learning
models.authors: Juno C. L. Chan, Lorena Magaña Zertuche, Jose María Ezquiaga, Rico K. L. Lo, Luka Vujeva, Joey Bowman
models.venue: arXiv preprint (no journal reference on arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv 2511.07186 (v2, PRD 8cz1-kl6n; full text read; P-P plots and Bayes factor distribution figures not rendered).
models.architecture: DINGO-lensing: neural posterior estimation (simulation-based inference) following DINGO. A dual network: an embedding network (first layer a 128-dimensional SVD-based compression of the frequency-domain strain, followed by residual blocks) conditioning a normalizing flow (neural spline coupling flow) that outputs 17-dimensional posteriors (point-mass lens parameters plus 15 binary parameters). Separate lensed and non-lensed networks; Bayes factor from importance sampling of each.
models.inputs: Frequency-domain whitened strain from H1 and L1 (8 s, 20-1024 Hz; NRSur check 20-512 Hz) with the O5 design ASD (Gaussian stationary noise), assuming a lens with two overlapping images and a constant pi/2 relative phase (type I/II images); waveform model IMRPhenomXPHM.
models.data: Training set 5e6 simulated waveforms from priors in Table I (2% held out for test), stored in SVD basis. Validation: 1e3 lensed injections (P-P), point-mass lens masses 500-1500 Msun, impact parameter 0-1.5; 2,561 lensed and 10,858 non-lensed simulated events (volume-uniform 1-15 Gpc, chirp mass 30-60 Msun, network SNR>8) for Bayes factor/background study.
models.training: Two-stage: Stage 0 SVD layer frozen, 300 epochs, Adam lr 7e-5, cosine scheduler; Stage 1 all layers unfrozen, 150 epochs, lr 1e-5; batch size 4096; ~10 days on one NVIDIA A100 PCIe; stopped at epoch 450. Non-lensed model trained likewise.
models.results: Posteriors well calibrated (P-P; KS p-values per parameter shown in Fig. 2, e.g. Mc 0.885, q 0.952, dL 0.148, theta_jn 0.056, a1 0.020, tc 0.657) and agree with bilby on a representative event (SNR 16.18, sampling efficiency 2.3%). Inference time reduced from weeks to tens of seconds per event. 2% of non-lensed simulations have B_lens>0; 53% of lensed simulations have B_lens>5. Sampling efficiencies after importance sampling 1e-4 to 0.1.

models.access: Open arXiv 1909.06367 (full text read; tables read in text, figures not rendered). PRD 100, 103025.
models.architecture: Fully connected ANN classifier. Pure-signal network: dense layers with batch norm, dropout, ReLU, softmax output over the number of sky sectors (18, 50, 128 shown). Noisy-signal network: six 200-unit dense layers (Dense1 4,400 params; Dense2-5 40,200 each; Dense6 25,728 to 128 sectors) each followed by batch normalisation (800 params), ReLU, dropout; softmax output. Keras (TensorFlow), Adam, categorical cross-entropy, early stopping.
models.inputs: Hand-engineered features from three detectors (H1, L1, V1): arrival-time delays and maximum cross-correlation values of the time series and their Hilbert-transform analytic signals (amplitude/phase near merger), normalised (x-mu)/sigma; features computed on 0.25 s strain at 2048 Hz.

Pure signal: 12,000 samples (10,800 train / 1,200 test). Noisy: 200,000 samples (160,000 train, 20,000 or 40,000 validation, 4,000 test) at injection SNR [50-55], [20-35], or [10-110] with curriculum learning.

Curriculum SNR 10-110 gives 65% (94.5% within one sector) at 128 sectors tested on SNR 20-35. models.title: Rapid localization of gravitational wave sources from compact binary coalescences using deep learning
models.authors: Chayan Chatterjee, Manoj Kovalam, Linqing Wen, Damon Beveridge, Foivos Diakogiannis, Kevin Vinsen
models.access: Open arXiv 2207.14522 (v2; ApJ 959, 42/ 2023). Text read; Figs. 3-8 (skymaps, area histograms, P-P) not rendered, so no numbers read from figures.
models.architecture: GW-SkyLocator: conditional normalizing flow. Features from the S/N time series via a ResNet-34 (2D-conv stem, 3 residual units with 32 filters, 4 with 64, 6 with 128..., kernel 3, batch norm, ReLU) and a fully connected channel for the intrinsic parameters (m1, m2, spins) of the matched filter; concatenated and used to condition a Masked Autoregressive Flow (stacked MADE units with batch norm) mapping a multivariate Gaussian to the posterior over (alpha, delta) (alpha decomposed into sin/cos for cyclicity). Loss: negative log-likelihood (cross entropy). Posterior sampled (5000 samples), a Gaussian KDE (bandwidth 0.02) evaluated on BAYESTAR-style adaptive HEALPix mesh.
models.inputs: Complex matched-filter S/N time series rho(t) from H1, L1, V1 of the optimal template (training) or best template (testing), short (about 0.2 s?) windows, plus the intrinsic parameters of the template. The S/N series is available from search pipelines (low-latency compatible).
models.data: 5e5 training injections and 2000 test injections for each of BBH, BNS, NSBH; BBH masses 10-80 Msun (Salpeter IMF), BNS 1-2.5 Msun, NSBH 1.0-2.5 / 10-80 Msun; network S/N 8-40 (uniform for training), test S/N from comoving-volume distribution (BBH z<=2.5); triggers need S/N>4 in at least two detectors and network S/N 9-40. Gaussian noise with Advanced LIGO PSD. For real events, retrained on injections in real O2 (GPS 1187008512-1187733618) / O3 (1242181632-1242705920) noise.
models.training: About 1.5 h on a P100 GPU per model; inference of 5000 samples a few ms; total with KDE and adaptive mesh ~1.2 s on average. Optimiser/learning rate/epochs/batch size not extracted from the main text.
models.results: Compared with BAYESTAR on 2000 injections each: medians of 90% credible area histograms close to BAYESTAR, but GW-SkyLocator areas larger at high S/N (>25) and fewer areas <10 deg2 (smallest 90% area with fixed KDE ~40 deg2); P-P plots show calibration; further optimisation said to be needed to match BAYESTAR. models.architecture: AWaRe (v1 here): denoising autoencoder with a CNN encoder and bidirectional-LSTM decoder. Input 1 s strain at 2048 Hz split into 2063 overlapping 15-timestep subsequences; each passes a time-distributed encoder (BatchNorm, Conv1D 64, Conv1D 32, Conv1D 32 with ReLU, BatchNorm, dropout 22%, 2-head multi-head attention with 32 dims, flatten 480), then concatenated into bidirectional LSTM layers (32 units, tanh) and a dense output of the whitened waveform. Loss: MSE (Fractal Tanimoto term gave no gain).

Test: 1,000 injections in O3b noise, plus real events GW150914, GW151226, GW190412, GW190521.

models.results: Test overlaps: 86% of 1,000 injections (SNR 8-30) reach overlap >0.9; the example injection (SNR 12) gives overlap 0.91; most injections with SNR>12 have overlap >0.9 (text truncated). models.title: Learning Bayesian posteriors with neural networks for gravitational-wave inference

models.architecture: Percival: plain multilayer perceptron (8 hidden layers x 1024 units, leaky ReLU) mapping reduced-basis coefficients beta (d~200) to the parameters of one bivariate Gaussian (5 outputs, linear), a 3-component bivariate Gaussian mixture (18 outputs) or a softmax histogram. Priors p1 (Mc in [2.4,4.5]x10^5, eta in [0.2,0.25], rho in [8,16], non-spinning), p2 (adds chi2 in [-1,1]), p3 (rho=2). Fresh batch of 1e5 signals each epoch (effectively infinite set).

models.title: DANTE: A Reference-Guided Unsupervised Pipeline for Extended-Transient Anomaly Characterization in LIGO O4a
models.authors: Luca Cirfeta
models.venue: arXiv preprint (no journal reference on arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv v3 (27 pp, read for architecture, setup and results; later results/discussion pages skimmed only by keyword).
models.architecture: DANTE: frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 with registers (no fine-tuning of the backbone) gives 1,369 patch tokens (384-d, L2-normalised) per 518x518 Q-transform image; Layer 1 scores each patch by cosine similarity to a vector-quantised reference index (MiniBatchKMeans centroids) and averages the Top-k=68 (~5%) most novel patches (MIL pooling) against a per-detector P99 threshold; Layer 2 PCA (adaptive) + Dirichlet-process Bayesian GMM (full/tied/diag covariance by n) for taxonomy; Layer 3 cross-session single-linkage clustering on cosine similarity (rho_trans=0.75).
models.inputs: 32 s strain windows (4 s context each side), band-limited 10-2048 Hz, whitened with adaptive median Welch PSD, Q-transform rendered to 256x256 cividis image, resized to 518x518.
models.data: GWOSC O4a H1 and L1 (GPS 1368973312-1384525312, ~180 of 237 days; 72 sessions, ~20% effective duty cycle; L1/H1 CBC CAT1). References: Gravity Spy O3b catalogue (23 classes, ~13,000 tokens, 281 centroids) and a native O4a index (150,000 segments per detector, 205,350,000 tokens, K=1,216 centroids). Injection MDCs of synthetic morphologies (Sine-Gaussian blips etc.).
models.training: Label-free: no network training; k-means index, PCA/DPMM fitted per session; seeds fixed to 42; PyTorch 2.1.1/CUDA 11.8, A100/V100.
models.results: Mock-data challenge: global [CLS] scoring recall 0.00 at FPR 1% (1,417 injections, 8 families); MIL Top-k recall >98% for harmonic comb, 58% for scattered light, 0.00 for blips/asym-blips even at SNR~380-430; production O4a scan yielded 140 candidates (4 H1, 136 L1), of which 53 survive native-O4a recalibration; version-2/3 notes: boundary-context defect affects 169 of 10,429 windows (changes 120 class assignments, 97 routing decisions). models.authors: Robert E. Colgan, Zsuzsa Márka, Jingkai Yan, Imre Bartos, John N. Wright, Szabolcs Márka
models.venue: arXiv preprint (no journal reference on arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv v2 (16 pp, read through Results/Conclusion/Appendix; Fig. 5 page read visually). Published PRD 107, 062006 (2023).
models.architecture: Linear-filter ('LF') flat convolutional binary classifier on AUXILIARY channels (not strain): one learned length-T=96-sample filter per channel, cross-correlated with the channel, summed over channels with one bias per sample rate, then a sigmoid; elastic-net regularisation drives most filters to zero (automatic channel selection). Slight modification of the LF model of refs [42,43].
models.inputs: 39,147 normalised auxiliary (witness) channels at all sample rates (from ~250,000, excluding constant or strain-coupled channels), 96 samples per channel centred at time t (6 s for 16-Hz channels, 3/8 s for 256-Hz).
models.data: Real LIGO Livingston data, 1 Dec 2019 (scattered-light-rich day): train GPS 1259197952-1259247952 (3,555 scattered-light glitches), validation 1259247952-1259257952 (924), test 1259257952-1259267952 (1,016). Positives = Gravity Spy 'scattered light' glitches; negatives = random times with no Omicron glitch within 2 s, equal number. 5,499 of 6,515 Gravity Spy glitches that day were scattered light; 48,879 Omicron triggers SNR>=5.
models.training: Hyperparameter grid, best model by validation loss (0.0933); procedure as in ref [43]; elastic net sparsity. Optimiser, epochs and compute not stated in this paper.
models.results: Validation accuracy 97.0% (TPR 97.4%, TNR 96.6%); test accuracy 97.1% (TPR 98.4%, TNR 95.8%) with only 25 of 39,147 channels selected (Table I; mostly L1:SUS-ETMX reaction-mass OSEM channels, consistent with known back-scatter from the reaction mass). Of 43 false positives, as many as 30 show faint scattered-light signatures; excluding them TNR would be 98.7% and accuracy 98.6%. All-Omicron-glitch variant reaches only 82.8% validation accuracy.

models.title: Neural Importance Sampling for Rapid and Reliable Gravitational-Wave Inference
models.authors: Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonathan Gair, Michael Pürrer, Jonas Wildberger, Jakob H. Macke et al.
models.access: Open arXiv v2 (15 pp incl. supplement; main text and Tables I-II read, supplement skimmed).
models.architecture: Dingo-IS: amortised neural posterior estimation (conditional normalizing flow, group-equivariant NPE / GNPE, architecture and hyperparameters as Dingo ref [10]) used as the proposal for importance sampling with weights p(d|theta)p(theta)/q(theta|d); effective sample size n_eff, sample efficiency eps=n_eff/n and unbiased Bayesian-evidence estimate; phase phi_c sampled synthetically on a grid with cached modes.
models.inputs: Frequency-domain strain [20,1024] Hz, Delta f=0.125 Hz, two LIGO detectors (Virgo left for a later paper), identical conditioning to Dingo; PSD supplied per event.
models.data: Training simulations with IMRPhenomXPHM and SEOBNRv4PHM waveforms, m1,m2 in [10,120] Msun, spin magnitudes [0,0.99], O1 and O3 noise PSDs; separate O3 networks for distance priors [0.1,3], [0.1,6], [0.1,12] Gpc. Applied to 42 BBH events of GWTC-2/3 consistent with the mass prior and to two events (GW150914, GW151012) validated against LALInference MCMC and Bilby-dynesty.
models.training: Network architecture, hyperparameters and training algorithm unchanged from Dingo [10] (details in that paper); 1e5 proposal samples per event; inference on one A100 + 64 CPU cores: <1 h (IMRPhenomXPHM) or ~10 h (SEOBNRv4PHM, versus months with stochastic samplers).
models.results: GW150914 (IMRPhenomXPHM): mean JSD 2.2e-3 nat (Dingo) to 0.5e-3 (Dingo-IS) and log evidence -15831.87+-0.01 vs Bilby -15831.78+-0.10; GW151012: mean JSD 9.0e-3 to 0.7e-3. Median sample efficiency 10.9% (IMRPhenomXPHM) and 4.4% (SEOBNRv4PHM) over 42 events; ten-fold smaller evidence uncertainty than standard samplers; low eps flags glitches/OOD (blip glitch eps~0.001%, adversarial eps~0.01%).

models.title: DVGAN: Stabilize Wasserstein GAN training for time-domain Gravitational Wave physics
models.authors: Tom Dooney, Stefano Bromuri, Lyana Curier
models.venue: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (Big Data), pp. 5468-5477, Osaka
models.access: Open arXiv (v2); PDF downloaded and read in full (10 pages), Table I read from the rendered page.
models.architecture: DVGAN: a three-player Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty for fixed-length 1D signals. Generator: strided transposed convolutions (kernel 5, upsample stride 2, BatchNorm in the first layer, ReLU, linear output); 100-d Gaussian latent. Base discriminator mirrors the generator (about 4.1M parameters each, dropout, LeakyReLU, no BatchNorm). Auxiliary derivative discriminator (about 300k parameters, ~8% of the base) sees dx/dt of real and generated signals. Generator loss = 0.5*D1(x) + 0.5*D2(dx/dt).
models.inputs: 1 s segments at 1024 Hz (1024 samples) for the analytic and BBH sets, peak-normalised to 1; blip glitches at 4096 Hz, 938 samples (0.23 s).
models.data: Four datasets: Gaussian pulses, damped ringdowns (analytic burst proxies after McGANn), IMRPhenom BBH (30-70 Msun, zero spin, plus polarisation, power-law mass index 1.6), and real LIGO O2 blip glitches (H1/L1, Gravity Spy confidence >=0.9, from an earlier extraction/denoising pipeline, with the rROF denoising step replaced by two Savitzky-Golay filters of order 3, windows 21 and 11). Whether the blip morphology survives the smoothing was not investigated.
models.training: 500 epochs on 6000 samples, batch 512, RMSprop lr 1e-4, 5 discriminator updates per generator update, GP regularisation, eta1=eta2=0.5; TensorFlow/Keras; trained on LIGO Laboratory cluster. Hyperparameters chosen by trial and error; a vanilla two-player WGAN with the same base architecture is the ablation. 5 repeats per condition.
models.results: DVGAN lowers the discriminative score (|0.5 - holdout error| of an independent 2-layer 1D CNN, lower = less distinguishable) on all four datasets versus the WGAN (pulse 0.029 to 0.009, ringdown 0.041 to 0.017, BBH 0.499 to 0.199, blip 0.453 to 0.129). BBH match analysis (PyCBC bank of 20,000 waveforms, 20-80 Msun): mean max match equal (0.9918 vs 0.9917), RMSE 0.0486 to 0.0428, time shift 0.174 to 0.154 samples; both GANs' mass distributions differ from the training set (KS rejects at 95% every repeat). Loss curves (Fig 3) are more stable for DVGAN; T-SNE (Fig 5) shows closer match.
models.code: No code link in the paper. Keras/TensorFlow named. GitHub search found no DVGAN repo for this paper (the author's later glitchgan repo implements the conditional descendant cDVGAN).
models.gaps: Single architecture/hyperparameter set, no tuning of either model; no statistical test for the stability claim (Fig 3 is a single qualitative example); the discriminator score is the only fidelity number for the real-data case; blip smoothing unvalidated; no downstream detection or classification benefit shown; the GAN was not conditioned.

models.title: Time-Domain Synthesis of Gravitational-Wave Detector Glitches using Class-Conditional Derivative Generative Adversarial Networks
models.authors: Tom Dooney, Mees de Boer, Harsh Narola, Melissa Lopez, Stefano Bromuri, Daniel Stanley Tan, Chris Van Den Broeck
models.venue: arXiv 2606.27227v3 (14 Sep 2026); the code repository README states Phys. Rev. D 114, 082005 (2026), doi 10.1103/d5yf-3jb4 (not verified at the publisher)
models.access: Open arXiv (v3); PDF downloaded, text read for Sections I-V (22 pages); appendices and figures not individually inspected.
models.architecture: GlitchGAN = class-conditional DVGAN (cDVGAN): WGAN-GP (lambda 10) with generator G(z in R^100, one-hot class in R^7) and two 1D-convolutional critics. G: class vector projected to a 32-d embedding, concatenated with z, dense layer, reshape, five upsample-and-convolve blocks with BatchNorm and ReLU, to 8192 samples. D acts on the 8192-sample waveform, D_partial on the 8191-sample first difference; projection conditioning; generator loss averages both critics; 5 critic updates per generator update. Comparison model: latent diffusion transformer (autoencoder 8192x1 to 256x16).
models.inputs: 2 s windows at 4096 Hz (8192 samples) of DeepExtractor glitch reconstructions, per-sample normalised to [-1,1] and mean-subtracted; no SNR information learned (samples are rescaled to a chosen SNR after generation).
models.data: 31,511 DeepExtractor reconstructions of H1 and L1 glitches from LIGO O3a/O3b, covering 7 Gravity Spy classes (Whistle, Tomte, Scattered Light, Low-Frequency Burst, Koi Fish, Fast Scattering and Blip) selected at Gravity Spy confidence >=0.9 and SNR>=15; each class bootstrap-oversampled to 5000 (35,000 in all). Holdout model: 28,360 for training and 3,151 (10%, stratified) held out.
models.training: 500 epochs, batch 64, RMSprop lr 1e-4, NVIDIA A100 about 12 h; the released model is the epoch-210 checkpoint (chosen by eye, loss stability and UMAP overlap). No hyperparameter tuning; TensorFlow.
models.results: Gravity Spy classifies the injected GlitchGAN samples correctly 79.3% of the time (n=700) versus 89.6% for the real DeepExtractor reconstructions; UMAP shows substantial real/synthetic overlap except for Whistle. A CNN separates held-out real from generated glitches at 95.7% in clean data but only 66.0% once both are injected into design-PSD Gaussian noise at empirical per-class SNRs. In a 7-class classifier, GlitchGAN augmentation to 5000/class is significantly better than the unaugmented baseline only when real data are scarce (95 real samples: 91.0% vs 85.7%), and synthetic-only training (91.8%) is as good as that. Generation speed: 1000 glitches in about 22 s on a CPU.
models.code: https://github.com/tomdooney95/glitchgan: exists, no licence file, last push 2026-10-16, trained generator weights provided (weights/tensorflow/generator_210_keras3.keras); documentation on readthedocs per the README. Separate LaTeX-source repo tomdooney95/glitchgan_glitch_synthesis_2026. Training data come from DeepExtractor (tomdooney95/deepextractor, MIT).
models.gaps: Fixed-SNR and magnitude-only (Q-transform) validation; Whistle class partly fails; no phase-aware validation; epoch chosen partly on the same UMAP evidence used to claim fidelity; class-conditioning only (no SNR conditioning); no test of detection-pipeline impact (only glitch classification); the DiT baseline is a limited-effort comparison.

models.title: Gravitational-wave background detection using machine learning
models.authors: Hugo Einsle, Marie-Anne Bizouard, Tania Regimbau, Mairi Sakellariadou
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF downloaded and read (text of Secs I-VI, Figs 3 and 6 viewed; appendices A-B not read).
models.architecture: MSMHAutoencoder: a multi-scale multi-headed autoencoder (inception-style kernels 3/5/7, encoder depth 3, 64 base channels, skip connections) acting on M=12 consecutive spectra of N=1005 frequency bins. Encoder_total gives a noise+signal latent; Decoder_noise estimates the noise spectrum; Encoder_noise re-encodes it; a learned corrector C adds to (z_total - z_noise) to give the signal latent; Decoder_signal outputs the GWB spectrum. Followed by emcee MCMC (50 walkers, 2000 steps, 1000 burn-in) on a power-law BBH + flat cosmological Omega model, with dynesty evidences for Bayes factors.
models.inputs: Log10 cross-correlation spectra built from 2048 s segments (50% overlap) at 512 Hz; MCMC restricted to 10-100 Hz, Omega reference at 25 Hz.
models.data: Fully simulated A+ design-sensitivity Hanford/Livingston Gaussian noise (Virgo mentioned in the setup but the training is on LIGO noise); astrophysical BBH GWB from population-synthesis catalogues (IMRPhenomXPHM, mean inter-event time 25 s, the high end of the rate); cosmological GWB as correlated Gaussian noise with the overlap reduction function. Split: 47.4 days (37.9 train, 9.5 validation), separate 23.7-day test set.
models.training: Supervised with a physics-informed loss L = 0.5 L_spectral + 0.1 L_latent + 0.1 L_consist (second-derivative smoothness penalty, heavier penalty for false signal on noise-only samples); Adam lr 5e-5, batch 32, up to 2000 epochs, early stopping; curriculum learning on signal amplitude over 100 epochs (amplitude floor from 1e2 down to 1e-2). Hyperparameters hand-picked, not searched. Four sample categories (noise only, noise+cosmo, noise+astro, both).
models.results: With 23.7 days of test data and no signal-free calibration, a BBH GWB with Omega_BBH about 1e-9 at 25 Hz reaches log10 Bayes factor 3; in presence of that BBH background a cosmological component of Omega_0 about 1.3e-10 is distinguished (log10 BF_cosmo > 3), though its posterior spans about two orders of magnitude. Sensitivity improves as T^-1.6 for the first ~10 h of training data, then T^-0.2, reaching about 1e-9 in under 100 h; faster than the cross-correlation T^-0.5 scaling initially.
models.code: No repo for the method; the simulation code is cited at gitlab.et-gw.eu/osb/div10/mdc-generation (Einstein Telescope collaboration GitLab, access not checked). GitHub search found nothing.
models.gaps: Gaussian stationary noise only; BBH-only astrophysical background; no calibration of Bayes factors on noise-only data (no false-alarm study); Gaussian-likelihood MCMC on the network's own output with sigma from the network's variability; no real data; the ML sensitivity metric (MSE<0.01 on the predicted spectrum) differs from the cross-correlation SNR=1 reference.
models.adaptation_notes: Stochastic-background autoencoder on cross-correlation spectra.

suspected_errors_extracted: Sec V states the MSE threshold of 0.01 'represents a difference of about 3%' between target and prediction. The MSE is on log10 spectra, so sqrt(0.01)=0.1 dex, a factor of 1.26 (about 26%) in Omega, not 3%.

The abstract says 'log noise Bayes factor of 3' but the body uses log10(BF)>3 as 'decisive'; the base is ambiguous in the abstract. In addition no noise-only distribution of the Bayes factor is shown, so BF=3 is not calibrated to a false-alarm probability, yet Sec VI equates it with 'close to 5 sigma'.
Abstract says the cosmological component is measured 'using 47.4 days of training data' but the quoted detections are on a separate 23.7-day test set; 47.4 days is the training+validation volume.

Sec VI says the search sensitivity is 'two times higher' than the LVK 5e-10 estimate: the number (1e-9) is two times worse, so 'higher' is ambiguous. The comparison is also between a 2-sigma LVK number and a BF=3 criterion.

models.title: RNLE: Residual neural likelihood estimation and its application to gravitational-wave astronomy
models.authors: Mattia Emma, Gregory Ashton
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF downloaded; text read for Secs I-X in part (methods, toy model, configuration, conclusion read; the middle results sections VI-IX and Figs 1-2, 5-7 and later figures only read through text extraction, not visually).
models.architecture: RNLE: neural likelihood estimation of the residual (data minus signal model) rather than the full data. Conditional density estimator = sbi v0.22.0 default masked autoregressive flow (5 MAF transforms, MADE nets with 2 hidden layers of 50 units, ReLU), trained only on noise simulations or real noise segments, with a mock scale parameter sigma (prior U[0,2]) as the single conditioning parameter. At sampling time a waveform is generated from the signal prior, whitened and subtracted from the whitened time-domain data, and the flow evaluates the residual likelihood; dynesty via Bilby. Multi-detector likelihood is the product. An ensemble of retrained flows is combined with evidence weights.
models.inputs: 4 s time-domain strain at 4096 Hz, Tukey-windowed (roll-off 0.2 s), whitened in the frequency domain (20-2048 Hz mask) then inverse-FFTed and cropped around the signal.
models.data: Toy sine-Gaussian in white noise; simulated coloured Gaussian noise (design PSD, horizon 180 Mpc) with IMRPhenomPv2 injections (1D chirp mass, 10D, 11D aligned-spin two-detector, and 15D precessing analyses); real LIGO data with BBH injections into quasi-Gaussian segments, into highly non-Gaussian O3b segments, and around blip glitches (an O2 blip at GPS 1165578732.45, 549 Hz; 14,300 s of surrounding data for training; blip datasets built from Gravity Spy classes).
models.training: About 3000 noise simulations per likelihood adopted as the compromise (JS divergence to the Whittle posterior stabilises at about 2000 for the 1D chirp-mass case; training time runs from minutes at 2e3 to hours at 1e5 simulations); several optimisation seeds per dataset to quantify 'training noise'.
models.results: In Gaussian noise RNLE reproduces the Whittle-likelihood posteriors (JS divergence below the 10/N equivalence threshold, N samples per KDE) with fewer simulations than standard NLE in the toy model. In loud non-Gaussian transients the Whittle posteriors are biased and miss the injection, while RNLE recovers consistent posteriors if the training set matches the glitch class, frequency range and relative timing. Retraining on identical data gives substantial posterior scatter in non-Gaussian noise; evidence weighting often selects a single, sometimes biased realisation; convergence of evidences is not reached. RNLE is more expensive than regular sampling because it keeps the waveform cost plus a flow evaluation.
models.code: sbilby package (github.com/MattiaEmma2022/sbilby, MIT, last push 2026-01-19, 4 stars; pip install sbilby==0.0.1). No trained likelihoods (the flows are trained per analysis).
models.gaps: Evidence variance across seeds indicates the number of simulations is insufficient for non-Gaussian noise; the cost is higher than Whittle sampling; extended multi-parameter tests only injection-level; no population-level calibration (p-p plots) was identified in the text I read.
models.adaptation_notes: Residual neural likelihood estimation.

models.title: Improving the detection significance of gravitational wave transient searches with CNN models
models.authors: Johann Fernandes, Archana Pai, Koustav Chandra
models.access: Open arXiv; PDF downloaded and read in full (main text 12 pages; appendix A on PyCBC-HM reweighting not read); Figs 5-6 and Tables II-III viewed as rendered pages.
models.architecture: ImageNet-pretrained Inception-V3 fine-tuned as a multi-class signal/noise-transient discriminator, plus a dense layer with 30% dropout and softmax; classes are blip, low-frequency blip, tomte (and koi fish, whistle for PyCBC-HM), coloured Gaussian noise, and signal. The signal-class probabilities from H1 and L1, P_H1 and P_L1, form R_CNN = 0.5 ln[(P_H1/(1-P_L1))^2 + (P_L1/(1-P_H1))^2], added to the PyCBC ranking statistic (R = R_base + R_CNN, with optional thresholds alpha, beta).
models.inputs: Continuous wavelet transform (Gabor-Morlet) maps over a 200 ms window around the trigger, 15-512 Hz, one per detector.
models.data: Glitches from Gravity Spy (confidence >0.9): about 9000 images per class for PyCBC-IMBH; signals from a stochastic IMRPhenomXAS template bank, detector-frame total mass 100-600 Msun, q 1-10, aligned spins +/-0.9, optimal SNR 5-40 (inclination 60-120 deg for PyCBC-HM, 40,000-template bank at minimal match 0.97); O3 H1/L1 coloured Gaussian noise class. Test: first four 30-day O3a chunks (1 Apr - 24 Aug 2019), 25,000 SEOBNRv4_ROM injections per chunk, distances 0.5-11 Gpc (IMBH) or uniform in volume (HM, 75-105 deg).
models.training: Categorical cross-entropy, Adam, F1 on the validation set for early stopping, balanced classes; alpha=0, beta=0 for PyCBC-IMBH (no thresholds), alpha=9.8, beta=0 for PyCBC-HM so only about 200,000 of 5e7 background triggers need CWT maps.
models.results: Sensitive VT ratio (ML/base) at IFAR 10/100/1000 yr rises with total mass from about 1.06 to 1.4-1.7 for PyCBC-IMBH and from about 0.9-1.0 to 1.3-1.4 for PyCBC-HM (loss in the 100-200 Msun bin at 100 yr); the abstract quotes about 30% at a FAR of once per 100 yr. For real O3a events GW190521 rises from IFAR 2140.6 to >42,813 yr with PyCBC-IMBH (about 20 times), though 4 of 11 events drop.
models.code: No code or model link in the paper; GitHub search found nothing (not exhaustive).
models.gaps: No standalone classifier performance (F1, confusion matrix, ROC) is reported in the main text; aligned-spin quasi-circular signals only; single detector-pair time slides; lower-mass bins not covered; results shown for O3a chunks 1-4 only.
models.adaptation_notes: CNN re-ranking of PyCBC IMBH triggers via CWT maps; needs PyCBC search outputs.

Fig 6 (PyCBC-HM): the VT ratio at IFAR 100 yr is below the ratios at both 10 yr and 1000 yr in every mass bin (for example 0.87 vs 1.00 and 1.005 in [100,200)), a non-monotonic pattern the text does not explain (Fig 5 is monotonic).

models.title: Automatic classification pipeline for glitches in the Virgo detector
models.authors: Tiago Fernandes, Francesco Di Renzo, Antonio Onofre, Alejandro Torres-Forne, Jose A. Font
models.venue: arXiv preprint 2604.13687v2 (20 Aug 2026); published as doi 10.1103/ys5f-2yqk (journal not stated in the arXiv text)
models.access: Open arXiv (v2); PDF downloaded; text read for Secs I-IV (16 pages; appendices, figures and the deployment section not read in detail).
models.architecture: VIGILant pipeline. Two model families compared: tree-based (Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost) on Omicron trigger parameters (peak frequency, SNR, amplitude, duration and others), and fastai/PyTorch ResNet (ResNet18/34/50 searched) on encoded spectrogram images (0.5/2.0/... s Q-transform views in colour channels, as in Gravity Spy multi-view). Selected: ResNet34. A softmax-confidence threshold (2.5th percentile of validation confidence, 0.8543) sets a 'Low Confidence' class. Deployed with an interactive glitch dashboard.
models.inputs: Encoded multi-duration Q-transform spectrogram images per glitch (ResNet); Omicron parameters (trees).
models.data: Curated Virgo O3b dataset of 11,193 glitches from Gravity Spy labels, merged to 7 classes: Scattering 4000 (Paired Doves, Light Modulation, Scattered Light, LF Burst, LF Lines merged), Resonance Line 2000 (Whistle + Violin Mode merged), Tomte 1801, Blip 1156, No Glitch 1000, Extremely Loud 938, Koi Fish 298; 'None of the Above' dropped. Confidence-weighted random sampling from Gravity Spy; split 70/15/15 stratified (7835/1679/1679).
models.training: ResNet34, AdamW with 1-cycle schedule, 17 epochs, lr 7.98e-3, batch 32, cross-entropy; 100-trial Optuna search for ResNet and for the trees; training 940 s. Test set untouched until the end.
models.results: Test set (1679 glitches): ResNet34 F1 0.9772 and accuracy 0.9833 (28 misclassified), precision and recall above 0.95 for all 7 classes; validation F1/accuracy: DT 0.856/0.903, RF 0.893/0.924, XGBoost 0.901/0.930, ResNet 0.971/0.975. With the confidence threshold 46 test glitches (2.7%) are set aside as Low Confidence, about 70% of them reasonably so; of 100 out-of-domain glitches, 38% (Air Compressor) and 29% (32 Hz Blobs) fall below the threshold. Inference about 0.04 s per glitch on CPU. Deployed daily at Virgo since O4c.
models.code: Pipeline/code not released as a repo that I could find. The data-availability statement points to git.ligo.org/tiago.fernandes/virgo-o3b-classification (LIGO GitLab, access not checked); dashboard demo at tttiago.github.io/glitchgram (repo tttiago/glitchgram, no licence, last push 2026-10-01). No trained weights seen.
models.gaps: Merged label classes make the 7-class task easier and non-comparable to Gravity Spy 22-class scores; random (not time-blocked) split of glitches drawn without temporal constraints; ground truth is Gravity Spy machine+volunteer labels with admitted label errors; F1 averaging (macro vs weighted) is not stated; only 45 Koi Fish in test.

models.authors: Daniel George, Hongyu Shen, E. A. Huerta
models.venue: arXiv 1706.07446v1 (22 Jun 2017); published as Phys. Rev. D 97, 101501(R) (2018)
models.access: Open arXiv (v1, 28 pages incl. appendices); PDF downloaded and text read for Secs I-V, Tables 1 and A1 (partly), figure captions; confusion-matrix figures not viewed.
models.architecture: ImageNet-pretrained VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, Inception-V2 and Inception-V3, all layers fine-tuned; final fully connected layer replaced by a 22-way softmax layer, dropout layers added at the input and before the output, one extra layer after the first trainable convolution for ResNet. Trained CNNs can be truncated (Inception-V3, 1008-d vector) and used as feature extractors for t-SNE and unsupervised clustering (Appendix C, proof of concept).
models.inputs: Gravity Spy spectrogram images (481x575x3), downsampled to 224x224x3 or 299x299x3. VGG/ResNet use the 2.0 s view only; Inception models use the 1.0/2.0/4.0 s grayscale views encoded into the three colour channels.
models.data: Gravity Spy O1 dataset, 22 classes, about 8500 hand-labelled samples (version as of 19 Apr 2017: 1080Lines and 1400Ripples added, about 300 extra Violin Mode); random 80/20 per-class train/test split, no validation set. models.results: Best top-1 test accuracy 98.84% (ResNet50 and InceptionV3), 100% top-5 (ResNet50, InceptionV2, InceptionV3); previous CNN from scratch retrained on the same split reaches 96.70% (20 classes 96.72%). models.title: Deep Learning for Real-time Gravitational Wave Detection and Parameter Estimation with LIGO Data
models.authors: Daniel George, E. A. Huerta
models.venue: NIPS 2017 Workshop on Deep Learning for Physical Sciences (DLPS), arXiv 1711.07966v2
models.access: Open arXiv (v2); PDF downloaded and read in full (7 pages); Fig 1 viewed from the rendered page.
models.architecture: Deep Filtering: a classifier 1D CNN and a predictor 1D CNN, both with 4 convolution layers (64, 128, 256, 512 filters; kernels 16, 16, 16, 32; dilations 1, 2, 2, 2; stride 1), max pooling 4/stride 4, ReLU, two dense layers (128, 64), softmax output for the classifier; each about 23 MB. Sliding window of 1 s with a 0.2 s step; the predictor (masses) is run on windows the classifier flags; multi-detector coincidence is applied per detector stream.
models.inputs: 1 s whitened strain (whitened with the average PSD of the real noise at that period), per detector.
models.data: Real O1 LOSC noise: 4096 s per detector around GW151226 and LVT151012 for training/validation, around GW150914 for testing. About 2500 EOB BBH templates (5-75 Msun in 1 Msun steps; test templates offset by 0.5 Msun) injected into noise. Plus sine-Gaussian glitches (simulated), eccentric Einstein Toolkit/ENIGMA waveforms (e 0.1-0.2) and SXS spin-precessing waveforms as unseen test classes.
models.training: Curriculum learning from matched-filter SNR at least 100 down to SNR 4-15; the predictor is trained first on mass labels, then copied and retrained as classifier with 90% pure-noise inputs (transfer learning); glitches are injected into training.
models.results: Sensitivity 100% for SNR above 10 at a false-alarm probability tuned under 1% per 1 s window, close to matched filtering with the same template bank (Fig 1); predictor mean relative mass error under 10% at high SNR (matched filtering over 10% with the same bank); GW150914 recovered with masses inside the published error bars and zero false alarms after coincidence. Evaluates in about 85 ms (CPU) and 540 microseconds (GPU) per second of data, versus over 2 s for matched filtering.
models.code: No code link; a demo notebook is cited at tiny.cc/CNN (not opened). GitHub search found no repo for the paper (not exhaustive).
models.gaps: False-alarm rate stated per window with no rate in Hz or per year and no background statistics beyond the quoted 1% (no long-duration noise-only test); sample size of glitch tests not given; single run of GW150914 used for the test noise; no comparison with a real search pipeline (only a same-bank matched filter); no hyperparameters beyond layer sizes.

models.title: Amplifying the Chirp: Using Deep Learning (U-Nets) to filter signal from noise in LIGO data
models.authors: Akshay Ghalsasi
models.venue: arXiv preprint (no journal reference on arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF read in full, text plus visual read of Table I and Fig 7).
models.architecture: Two-stage pipeline on CWT images. (1) A 6-level 2D U-Net (n0=32 filters doubling per level, 3x3 kernels, ReLU, strided convolutions in place of max-pooling, transposed-convolution upsampling with skip connections, final 1-filter conv) used as a denoising filter in two flavours: Noise2Clean (noisy CWT in, clean synthetic CWT out) and Noise2Noise (H1 CWT in, L1 CWT out and vice versa; two separate N2N U-Nets, one trained on signal-present data and one on noise-only data, whose outputs are differenced). (2) An ImageNet-initialised EfficientNetB7 (top replaced by a single-neuron classifier) fed a 3-channel image: U-Net-filtered H1, U-Net-filtered L1 and a product channel 2*H*L/max(H+L). The U-Net is frozen while the EfficientNet is trained.
models.inputs: Whitened (FFT divide by average noise-only PSD) and Tukey-windowed (alpha=0.2) 2 s, 2048 Hz H1 and L1 strain, converted to magnitude of the complex CWT (phase discarded). Virgo channel dropped.
models.data: Kaggle G2Net competition set (560,000 labelled 2 s samples, half with a simulated BBH signal; only a random 1/4 = 140,000 used for the benchmark, 90/10 train/validation so ~14,000 validation samples; the full set is used for N2N training). Noise2Clean training uses 140,000 synthetic 2 s GGWD/PyCBC waveforms (70,000 per detector; m1,2 10-80 Msun, spin 0-0.998, SNR 10 then progressively lowered, merger placed 1.45-1.95 s; 130,000 train, 10,000 validation) added to noise-only samples drawn from the benchmark set.
models.training: N2C: iterate over synthetic set until validation RMSE converges, then lower the SNR by an O(1) factor and retrain (curriculum). Small Gaussian noise added to the clean target to avoid the trivial zero solution. N2N: 10 epochs, random swap of input/target detectors. EfficientNet: two regimes (last layer only vs all layers). Optimiser, learning rate, batch size and hardware not stated.
models.results: G2Net-subset validation AUC / accuracy (Table I): EfficientNet last-layer 0.7355 / 0.6788; EfficientNet all layers 0.8344 / 0.7657; U-Net N2C + EffNet last-layer 0.8206 / 0.7535; N2C + EffNet all 0.8329 / 0.7577; N2N + EffNet last-layer 0.8086 / 0.7497; N2N + EffNet all 0.8209 / 0.7604. The U-Net front end only helps when the backbone is frozen; with a fully trained EfficientNet it is slightly worse. Confusion matrices (Fig 7, threshold 0.5), as fractions of the validation set (TN/FP/FN/TP): fully trained EfficientNet 0.44/0.061/0.17/0.33; with N2C 0.41/0.089/0.15/0.35. The author concludes that the filter yields too many false positives.

No denoising overlap/match or SNR-gain number is reported despite the 'filter' framing: denoising quality is shown only as example CWT images (Figs 3, 4, 6). U-Net training hyperparameters, N2N filter sizes, and the SNR schedule are not given. Single run, no error bars; the 0.2 pp AUC differences are within plausible seed noise.

models.title: Using normal to find abnormal: AI-based anomaly detection in gravitational wave data
models.authors: Yi-Yang Guo, Soumya D. Mohanty, Xie Qunying, Yu-Xiao Liu
models.venue: arXiv preprint (no journal reference on arXiv record)
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF text read in full except appendices B and the figure gallery; Fig 16 and 17 read visually).
models.architecture: ABNORMAL: a dual-path iTransformer autoencoder that reconstructs statistical features of noise, not the time series. Two encoders (one for Gabor-filter-bank features, one for wavelet-filter-bank features), each three iTransformer layers (8 heads, feed-forward 2048, model dim 512, dropout 0.1, ReLU, rows of the feature matrix as tokens); latents concatenated into a shared space; two decoders, each an input projection, N=2 repeated blocks of (8-head attention, linear, ReLU, dropout 0.1) and an output projection, with separate heads rebuilding the GFB and WFB features. Anomaly score is the total reconstruction loss L_GFB + L_WFB (MSE on features).
models.inputs: Single-detector strain, band-limited to [30,1700] Hz at 4096 Hz sampling, lines removed with fixed notch filters. Two filter banks: 100 zero-phase FIR band-pass filters (order 1001, -3 dB bandwidth 47 Hz, 75% overlap, centres uniform in [30,1700] Hz) and a wavelet bank (Morlet, 400 scales 6.4-224, regrouped by inverse CWT into 5 band-passes). Each filtered segment is normalised by the median of the std of 20 blocks, then converted to features: block-wise mean and variance over Nblks blocks plus an Nblks-bin histogram. Short-timescale analysis: 5 s segments, Nblks=20; long-timescale: 20 s segments.
models.data: Training: 2000 unique 3600 s Gaussian noise realisations (each from its own PSD, a 5th-order log-frequency polynomial fit of the aLIGO ZDHP design PSD with +-2% parameter perturbation); validation 1000 more. Test: validation noise (false-alarm estimation) plus mock anomalous sets of 1600 realisations (200 each of 8 classes: 5 Gravity-Spy-like short glitch classes A-E, linear chirp, quadratic chirp, IMRPhenomD BBH) at fixed SNR 5/10/15/20 or log-uniform SNR in [10,20], each with its own unseen perturbed PSD. Real data: H1 and L1 O1, O2, O3a, O3b (546 min = 9.1 h of coincident data for the headline table; 88.74 h in the conclusion); per-run thresholds from run-matched mock noise built from the lowest-loss 1000 s segment's PSD.
models.training: Adam, gradient clipping at 1.0, staged schedule: epochs 1-20 WFB path only (lr 5e-4), 21-70 GFB path only (lr 1e-4), alternate to epoch 140, then all parameters (lr 1e-4) to epoch 300 with early stopping (no improvement of the 10-epoch rolling validation loss over 50 epochs); terminated at epoch 205, best model epoch 197. Trained only on simulated noise; never retrained per run (only the loss distribution is recomputed).
models.results: On mock data (Gaussian noise, ZDHP-like PSD): per-class AUC in Table I (e.g. Glitch A 0.671/0.990/1.000/1.000 at SNR 5/10/15/20; linear chirp 0.554/0.555/0.747/0.920; IMRPhenomD 0.561/0.855/0.993/1.000). At the working threshold (FAP ~0.5% per 5 s segment = FAR ~1e-3 /s ~ 3.6 /h) the SNR needed for 50% detection is 8.28-14.63 for the glitch classes and IMRPhenomD (12.17), 21.8-22.3 for chirps; 90% needs 13.0-26.2 (Table II). Real signals: ~90% of 4-OGC BBH events with single-detector SNR>~15 detected; detection fraction vs SNR for real GW events in real noise tracks mock-in-mock within bootstrap errors (Fig 17). Real-noise anomaly rates in 546 min: 270 detected (29.7 /h) against 3.6 /h nominal; per-run rates 3.5-40.9 /h (Table III).
models.code: No code or data statement found in the paper (reference list only cites pycbc and others). GitHub searches (ABNORMAL, authors, topic) found no repository.
models.gaps: Detection threshold (FAP 0.5% per 5 s) is far above GW-search FAR (3.6 /h), so efficiencies are for a coarse anomaly flag, not a search statistic; no ROC at low FAP. Real-data false-alarm rate is set by mock-noise matching and mode alignment of the loss distribution, not measured. No glitch/real-anomaly classification or accuracy against Gravity Spy labels; anomalies labelled by visual inspection only. Single detector only, no coincidence. Fig 18-21 (anomaly examples) and Appendix B (line removal) skimmed, not extracted.
