models.architecture: Multi-head CNN (6.35M parameters): shared encoder of six conv blocks (channels 64,128,256,512,512,256; kernels 7,5,5,3,3,3; GroupNorm(32); max-pool after layers 0,2,4; global average pool; dropout 0.3), a detection head (256-128-1, sigmoid) and five frequency heads (256-128-2 each, outputting normalised frequency and aleatoric sigma; only three supervised: fpeak, f1, p1). Ensemble of 5 networks with different seeds; epistemic uncertainty from ensemble standard deviation. Focal loss (gamma 2) for detection plus MSE on frequency (weight 10).
models.inputs: 100 ms segments sampled at 16384 Hz, whitened with a median-Welch PSD (floor 5% of median PSD, gain cap 20x), 8th-order Butterworth band-pass 2-4 kHz, STFT (10 ms Hann, 75% overlap; about 37 frames x 64 bins) split into four 500 Hz sub-band channels (centres 2250/2750/3250/3750 Hz); global normalisation.
models.data: Entirely synthetic. Signals: damped sinusoid h = A exp(-t/tau) sin(2 pi fpeak t + phi), fpeak 2-4 kHz, tau 15-80 ms, 'parameterised from' 590 CoRe BNS waveforms (254 configurations, 18 EOS) split by waveform 413/88/89 (70/15/15%); each waveform gets 1000 randomised variations (413,000 train, 88,000 val, 89,000 test). Noise: synthetic 'O4-like' (non-stationary PSD +-15%, spectral lines, 15% Student-t df=3 mixture, scattered-light transients, flat ~5e-24 /sqrt(Hz) above 2 kHz) with injected Gravity Spy glitch morphologies for 22 of 23 O3 classes (30% train rate). SNR labels 5-20 computed on raw time-domain waveforms before whitening. No real detector strain used.
models.training: AdamW lr 1e-4, wd 1e-5, cosine annealing, up to 100 epochs with early stopping (patience 15; best epoch mean 24.6 +- 10.4, about 37 epochs run); batch 50% signal / 50% noise-only; gradient clip 1.0; about 4 h per ensemble member on a laptop RTX 4070. Training uses harder augmentation than validation/test (PSD scaling +-30% vs +-20%, 30% white-noise bursts vs 15%, +-10 deg phase vs +-5 deg, +-6% time warp vs none), so validation loss (0.0360) is below training loss (0.0576).
models.results: Synthetic test set (89,000): ROC AUC 0.999999 and 99.998% efficiency at 1% false-positive rate (1 missed of 44,570 signals); frequency MAE 53.0 Hz (std 38.9 Hz) on the comprehensive test set, 48.6 Hz on 'direct-comparison subsets'; ensemble latency 3.04 ms (5 x 0.5 ms). Baselines: Lorentzian-template matched filter 1134.2 Hz MAE at 0.65 ms; Bayesian PE quoted from literature at 20 Hz and 3600 s. FAR calibration: 15 false alarms in 5000 noise-only samples (0.3%), quoted as 0.03 /yr after assuming 10 triggered searches per year. Frequency uncertainty vs labelled SNR rises (slope +0.25, R2 0.935), opposite to Cramer-Rao.
models.code: https://github.com/sathnidu9/postmerger-gw-eos-inference (MIT, created 2025-12-28, last push 2025-12-30); contains only LICENSE, postmerger_clean.py and validation_clean.py, no weights, no data.
models.gaps: No real detector data; no efficiency-vs-SNR curve (the paper itself says the SNR labels are not the effective SNR in the processed input); the 'direct-comparison subset' is not defined; test signals are 1000 variations of 89 parametric damped sinusoids, not NR waveforms; no per-segment-to-annual FAR mapping beyond an assumed 10 triggers/yr.

suspected_errors_extracted: Metrics are saturated (AUC 0.999999, 99.998% at 1% FPR): the signals are damped sinusoids at SNR 5-20 in a band-limited 2-4 kHz spectrogram, and the 89,000 test samples are 1000 augmentations of only 89 waveforms, so the test set is not independent in the way its size suggests; the author's explanation (harder training than validation) shows the validation set is easier than training, not that the result transfers to real noise.

Two operating points are mixed: the headline efficiency is at 1% FPR, but the FAR calibration uses a different threshold (geometric mean of mean probabilities) that gives 0.3% FPR; the abstract's '1% false alarm rate' is a per-segment fraction, not a rate.
The abstract's 48.6 Hz is on 'direct-comparison subsets' that are never defined; the same model has 53.0 Hz MAE on the full test set (Sec. 5.1), so the headline number is the more favourable one.
Sec. 4.1 says AUC is 'calculated to FPR 10^-3' but reports 0.999999 as ROC AUC; a partial AUC to 1e-3 cannot be compared with a full AUC.

Positive slope of uncertainty vs SNR (+0.25) is explained by SNR labels being computed before whitening/band-pass/normalisation; this means no usable SNR axis exists for the paper's efficiency or accuracy claims.
Text says training waveforms come from CoRe (590 waveforms) but Eq. 1 generates damped sinusoids from catalogue parameters, so no numerical-relativity waveform is ever injected.

models.title: Gravitational Wave Signal Denoising and Merger Time Prediction By Deep Neural Network
models.authors: Yuxiang Xu, He Wang, Minghui Du, Bo Liang, Peng Xu
models.access: Open arXiv v2 (PDF read in full, 13 pp; Figs. 5 and 6 viewed).
models.architecture: WaveUformer-CNN. WaveUformer: WaveUNet-style 1D encoder-decoder (12 down-sampling and 12 up-sampling blocks with skip connections) with a Sepformer-style separator in the bottleneck (two Sepformer blocks, each 8 IntraTransformer + 8 InterTransformer layers on chunked features) predicting a multiplicative GW feature mask. A small CNN (reusing the down-sampling blocks, then average pooling and two linear layers) regresses the time to merger from the denoised waveform. Detection rule: overlap between the denoised outputs of two windows one hour apart exceeds a threshold.
models.inputs: 30-day whitened Taiji A/E TDI data at 0.1 Hz (259,200 samples) from the inspiral phase, window slid by 1 hour.
models.data: Simulated Taiji data: MBHB signals from IMRPhenomD via bbhx (TDI-processed) with chirp mass 1e5-1e7 Msun (Table I), merger within 0-10 days after the 30-day window end, optimal SNR 10-50 injected into Gaussian Taiji noise (acceleration + OMS noise PSD, TDI A/E). 50,000 training samples; tests of 5000 samples per chirp mass (1e5, 1e6, 1e7 Msun), SNR uniform 10-50; detection tests balanced 2500 noise / 2500 signal per chirp mass.
models.training: MSE loss for both networks (label = noise-free template for denoising; time to merger for prediction); Adam, warmup (3 epochs, 1e-5 to 1e-3) plus cosine annealing, 100 epochs; about 10 h on three A100 40 GB.
models.results: Denoising: 91.98% of denoised test samples have overlap >=0.99 with the template and 95.82% have SNR loss <=5%. Detection (threshold about 0.977): 0 false positives in 2500 noise samples per chirp mass; TPR 98.64% / 99.48% / 99.68% for chirp mass 1e5 / 1e6 / 1e7 (mean 99.27%, called 'accuracy' in the paper). Merger time: 89.1% of test samples within 24 h absolute error; mean error 10.65 +- 12.57 h for all signals within 10 days of merger, falling to 3.42 +- 4.42 h within 1 day.
models.code: No code link in the paper; GitHub keyword search (WaveUformer etc.) found nothing.
models.gaps: Only stationary Gaussian simulated Taiji noise, no glitches/gaps, single source, SNR 10-50 only (same as training), no FAR per unit time (zero false positives in 2500), threshold chosen on the test sets.
models.adaptation_notes: Taiji MBHB denoising and merger-time prediction.

models.title: Self-supervised reconstruction of transients in data from space-borne gravitational-wave detectors
models.authors: Yuxiang Xu, Minghui Du, Bo Liang, Zihao Xiao, Tianyu Zhao, Peng Xu
models.venue: arXiv preprint (v1, 5 Sep 2026; no journal reference)
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF read in full, 13 pp; text read, figures not inspected because the quoted numbers are stated).
models.architecture: Noise2Noise-inspired self-supervised time-domain extractor: a 5-stage strided-conv encoder (kernel 8, stride 4, initial 48 channels doubled each stage, ReLU + pointwise conv + GLU) with 4x sinc up-sampling of the input, a 2-layer bidirectional LSTM bottleneck, a mirrored decoder with skip connections, sinc down-sampling to the original length. Training objective: predict one of two complementary random neighbouring-sample half-rate views from the other (MSE) plus a consistency regulariser (gamma=1) tying it to the full-rate output. No clean targets; no transient templates at inference.
models.inputs: One-day segments of whitened Taiji A2-channel TDI data at 0.1 Hz (8640 samples), normalised by sample standard deviation.
models.data: Simulated with the Taiji Data Challenge Triangle toolkit: Gaussian ACC + OMS instrumental noise (numerical unequal-arm orbit, TDI). Training set: only MBHB signals (IMRPhenom via BBHx/WF4PY) injected at optimal SNR 30-50 into noise (training-set size not stated). Test sets: 1000 samples per class at each of SNR 30, 40, 50 for MBHBs, LPF-like GRS acceleration glitches (dv 1.18-2.2e-12 m/s) and cosmic-string cusp bursts, all with TDC II galactic-binary foreground and SGWB added (never in training). A 30-day stream with 30 injected glitches for the subtraction test.
models.training: Adam, max lr 3e-4, 1000-step linear warmup then cosine decay, 100 epochs, batch 64, four A100 40 GB for about 6 h.
models.results: MBHB recovery: 94.8 / 97.3 / 98.4% of samples exceed overlap 0.9 at SNR 30 / 40 / 50. Cross-morphology (not in training): glitches 66.2 / 79.6 / 81.1% above overlap 0.8; cosmic-string bursts 87.1 / 96.8 / 98.3% above 0.8. Conditional subtraction in a 30-day stream: injected-anomaly power suppressed by 69.8% over 1e-5-5e-2 Hz and by 87.1% in the glitch band 1e-4-1e-3 Hz (residual 12.9% of injected power; contaminated-stream power 14.13x baseline reduced to 2.71x).
models.code: No code for the method. Data simulators referenced: github.com/TriangleDataCenter/Triangle-Simulator and Triangle-BBH (GPL-3.0, actively maintained); TDC II data on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15532090.
models.gaps: Training-set size and number of training steps not stated; no detection/FAR metric (extraction only); test SNR 30-50 only, simulated Gaussian instrumental noise, no gaps or non-stationarity (acknowledged); overlap thresholds (0.9, 0.8) are chosen post hoc per class.

models.title: Use of Excess Power Method and Convolutional Neural Network in All-Sky Search for Continuous Gravitational Waves
models.authors: Takahiro S. Yamamoto, Takahiro Tanaka
models.access: Open arXiv v2 (PDF read, 14 pp; Fig. 5-7 page viewed).
models.architecture: Pipeline: Earth-rotation time resampling at coarse sky grid points, short-time Fourier transform, a Fourier transform over time of one frequency bin ('l-domain' signal concentrated in about 10^3 bins), excess-power selection of candidate chunks, then a 1D CNN that regresses the source sky position (delta-n_x, delta-n_y) from a 2048-sample complex chunk, to shrink the region followed up by coherent matched filtering. CNN: six 1D conv layers (16,16,8,8,4,4 kernels; 2 to 64/128/256 channels), ReLU, three max-pool layers, fully connected head (Table I).
models.inputs: Complex l-domain chunk (real and imaginary channels, length 2048) of the time-resampled, STFT'd strain.
models.data: Fully simulated stationary Gaussian noise, single detector (LIGO Hanford geometry) with 100% duty cycle, observation 2^24 s, 1024 Hz, no spin-down, psi, iota, phi0 fixed and assumed known, one sky patch and a single 100 Hz frequency bin. Training: 200,000 waveforms, validation 10,000; amplitude log10 h0hat uniform in [-2.1,-1.0] each step with fresh noise.
models.training: MSE regression, Adam, batch 256, GeForce 1080Ti, PyTorch; hyper-parameters chosen by smallest validation loss.
models.results: Sensitivity depth D95% of about 80 for a feasible computing budget (all-sky coherent cost 2.2e8 s at 1 PFlops infeasible); D95% from the model ranges roughly 20-120 across (FAP_EP, r_NN) (Fig. 6); CNN processes 1e4 candidates in 1.4 s; reduces the follow-up sky region by two orders of magnitude; injection test recovers p_det = 0.935-0.98 vs the 0.95 target. Overall false alarm probability set to 0.01.
models.code: No code link in the paper; GitHub keyword searches found no repository.
models.gaps: Idealised (Gaussian, single detector, no gaps, no spin-down, fixed nuisance parameters); only one sky patch/frequency bin was trained and tested; the injection test skips the coherent follow-up stage; no actual trial on real data.

models.title: The response of the Convolutional Neural Network to the transient noise in Gravitational wave detection
models.authors: Chao Zhan, Mingzhen Jia, Cunliang Ma, Zhongliang Lu, Wenbin Lin
models.venue: arXiv preprint (manuscript formatted for Commun. Theor. Phys.; no journal reference on INSPIRE)
models.access: Open arXiv (PDF read in full, 7 pp; Figs. 2-8, 11 viewed).
models.architecture: The 1D CNN of Gabbard et al./ Ref. [37]: 6 conv layers (8,8,16,16,32,32 filters), three max-pool layers, dropout, two 64-unit hidden layers, 2-way softmax, ELU; input 8192 samples (1 s at 8192 Hz). Not new; the paper probes a trained classifier.
models.inputs: 1 s whitened (Advanced LIGO design PSD) single-detector time series, 8192 Hz.
models.data: Simulated: Gaussian 'LIGO-like' noise (design-sensitivity PSD) vs noise plus IMRPhenomD BBH signals with masses 5-95 Msun (log-uniform), no spins, optimal SNR scaled to a target (SNR 10 for the quoted test), isotropic sky; test glitches (1000 samples each) Gaussian (duration 1-10 ms), sine-Gaussian and ring-down with f0 uniform in 40-1500 Hz, Q in 2-20, injected at glitch-to-noise ratio 1-10. Training-set size not stated; 1500 test samples (750 + 750) at SNR 10.
models.training: Binary classifier trained without glitches (about 18 epochs shown in Fig. 4, final accuracy about 0.95-0.96); also retrained with 'inverse-GW' augmentation (inverted signal+noise labelled noise).
models.results: Classifier 96.4% accurate at SNR 10 (recall 98.4%, false positive rate 5.6% on the 750-noise test). Sine-Gaussian and Gaussian glitches are judged as noise with probability about 0.97-0.99; ring-down glitches about 0.88-0.94. By glitch centre frequency, ring-down glitches at 40-300 Hz are judged noise only about 70% of the time (false alarm about 30%), consistently with filtered-GW tests (30-60 Hz band: 91.4% called GW; 200-4096 Hz: 47.3%). Inverse-GW augmentation raises the RD noise probability by about 5% and lowers G/SG by about 1%.
models.code: No code link; only PyCBC (github.com/gwastro/pycbc) is cited.
models.gaps: Training-set size, SNR range of training, noise-only false alarm baseline and the exact SNR-bin numbers are not stated; the response study uses synthetic glitches only and a single trained network.
models.adaptation_notes: Glitch-response probe of a Gabbard-type CNN.

suspected_errors_extracted: Fig. 2 caption calls 96.4% 'sensitivity', but from the printed matrix (708/42/12/738) 96.4% is the accuracy ((708+738)/1500); the sensitivity (recall) is 98.4%.

The matrix implies a false positive rate on pure noise of 5.6% (42/750), yet the glitches are said to have false alarm probability 'close to that of the LIGO-like noises' while Fig. 6 gives sine-Gaussian/Gaussian false alarms of only about 1-3%; the noise baseline against which glitches are compared is never stated.
Abstract says the misjudged-as-GW probability 'may even exceed 30%', while Fig. 7 gives 0.70 judged as noise at 40-300 Hz (about 30%, not clearly above).
Text on the Fig. 3 'SNR' axis and the glitch 'SNR' axis in Fig. 6 are different quantities (glitch-to-noise ratio is not defined as optimal SNR); the SNR-bin mapping in Fig. 3 is approximate.

models.title: Detecting Gravitational-waves from Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals using Convolutional Neural Networks
models.authors: Xue-Ting Zhang, Chris Messenger, Natalia Korsakova, Man Leong Chan, Yi-Ming Hu, Jing-dong Zhang
models.venue: Phys. Rev. D 105, 123027 (2022); arXiv:2202.07158 (the PDF read is arXiv v1, 15 Feb 2022, so the published text may differ)
models.access: Open arXiv; v1 PDF read in full (text plus the figure pages 4-5 and 8-9 rendered). No code or weights released that I could find.
models.architecture: Plain 1D (1x k kernels on a 2-channel input) CNN binary classifier (signal+noise vs noise) for a 3-month TianQin EMRI search. Input 2 x 262144 matrix (TianQin treated as two orthogonal Michelson channels I and II, no TDI, long-wavelength approximation). Table III: Conv(32 filters, 1x34, ReLU) -> pooling (1x8) -> Conv(16, 1x8) -> pooling (1x6) -> Conv(16, 1x6) -> pooling (1x4) -> Flatten -> Dense 128 (ReLU) -> Dense 32 (ReLU) -> Dense 2 (softmax). Kernel size 34 was found by trial and error after starting from 5 (following earlier GW-CNN studies). Hyper-parameter search is not described beyond 'trial and error'.
models.inputs: Whitened (frequency-domain, using the analytic TianQin noise PSD, Tukey window alpha=1/4 on return to the time domain) strain of channels I and II, 7,864,320 s (3 months) sampled at 1/30 Hz (262144 samples), frequency band 1e-4 to 1 Hz. Gaussian stationary noise only; no gaps, no glitches, no foreground (galactic binaries) and no other sources.
models.data: Fully simulated. Noise sampled from the one-sided analytic TianQin PSD (Eq. 1: Sa=1e-30 m2 s-4/Hz, Sx=1e-24 m2/Hz, Larm=sqrt(3)e8 m). Signals: Analytic Kludge (AK) EMRIs with a 10 Msun compact object; MBH mass log-uniform in 1e4-1e7 Msun, spin uniform [0,1], plunge eccentricity uniform [0,0.2], isotropic sky/orientation angles, merger fixed at the end of the 3-month window; each signal rescaled to a target SNR uniform in [50,120] (distance irrelevant). Training: 2.5e5 signal+noise samples (noise-only count not stated; mini-batches 50/50). Seven test groups (Table IV): (1) AK like training, 500 signals; (2) AK with astrophysical population M12, SNR>50, 500; (3) AAK waveforms with training distribution, 500; (4) fixed SNR 10..130, 1000 each; (5) MBH mass scan at z=0.1/0.2/0.3; (6) spin scan, M=1e6; (7) redshift scan for three MBH types (1000 per point). Number of noise-only test samples used for FAP is not stated.
models.training: Binary cross-entropy (Eq. 9), Nadam optimiser, mini-batch 56 (28 signal + 28 noise), up to 300 epochs, early stopping when validation accuracy does not increase for 50 epochs; about 2 h per epoch, 10.5 days total on one V100 16 GB (Keras 2.2.4, TensorFlow; the footnote's 'Tensorflow 1.1.18' is not a real version). Training samples SNR 50-120 only (lower limit set by I/O and storage, not by choice).
models.results: On test data distributed like the training set (AK, SNR 50-120) the TAP is about 0.92 (text) at FAP 1% (the ROC in Fig 3 reads about 0.88); with an astrophysical (M12) population, whose SNRs cluster just above 50, the TAP at 1% FAP is stated as ~75% but reads ~0.56 off Fig 3; with AAK waveforms (never seen in training) the TAP at 1% FAP reads ~0.81. TAP versus SNR (Fig 4a): at FAP 0.1, 0.72 at SNR 50, 0.96 at 70, ~1.0 from 90; at FAP 0.01, 0.45 at SNR 50, 0.86 at 70, ~1.0 from 100. Sensitivity peaks for MBH mass about 1e5.5-1e6 Msun (TAP 0.76 at z=0.1, FAP 0.1) and falls to ~0.07-0.13 at z=0.3; almost no dependence on spin. Inference takes under a second per 3 months of data. Conclusion: a proof of principle for SNR>50 EMRIs in Gaussian noise; the authors say a template bank of ~1e40 templates would be needed for matched filtering.
models.code: No code, data or weights linked in the paper (no code-availability statement). GitHub searches (title, first author, 'EMRI CNN', 'TianQin deep learning', arXiv id) found nothing by these authors. The nearest hit, AminBoumerdassi/EMRI_signal_detection (convolutional autoencoders, last push 2024, no licence declared), is a different group's different method and is not linked to this paper.
models.gaps: Only proof of principle: Gaussian stationary noise, no TDI, no data gaps, no confusion foreground, SNR>=50 only in training; test efficiency below SNR 50 is extrapolation. Number of noise-only test samples (needed for the FAP down to 1e-3) is not stated; ROC has no repeat or uncertainty beyond a 1-sigma band of unstated origin. No comparison with any matched-filter or other search (the authors say none exists). No network-selection or hyper-parameter ablation; the CNN is applied to the full 3-month series, so no search over merger time or partial signals. AAK was only tested with an AK-trained network, not trained on AAK. Whether the 2.5e5 training count includes the noise-only half is unclear. TAP of Fig 4 b-d depends on SNR distribution induced by redshift, not fixed SNR.

models.title: Factorized neural posterior estimation for rapid and reliable inference of parameterized post-Einsteinian deviation parameters in gravitational waves
models.authors: Yong-Xin Zhang, Tian-Yang Sun, Chun-Yu Xiong, Song-Tao Liu, Yu-Xin Wang, Shang-Jie Jin, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
models.venue: Commun. Theor. Phys. 78 (2026) 115401; arXiv:2602.01319 (PDF read is v2, 30 Sep 2026)
models.access: Open arXiv; v2 PDF (19 pages) read in full, figure pages 7-10 rendered. No code or weights found.
models.architecture: Nine independent amortised neural-posterior-estimation (NPE) models, one per ppE (TIGER-style) deviation parameter dchi0..dchi7 (including the log terms dchi5l, dchi6l), each a conditional normalising flow: 10 stacked affine coupling layers, each with a sub-network of 5 hidden layers x 512 units. The data embedding is a 3-layer 1D CNN (downsampling) followed by a ResNet of 128 residual blocks (each two fully connected layers of 512 units, batch norm and dropout 0.1; Fig 2 calls this '256 layers'). A separate 2-layer MLP encodes the other (conditioning) parameters theta*_i; its output is concatenated with the data embedding and fed to the flow, so p(dchi_i | x, theta*_i) is learned. The joint posterior is approximated by a basic-parameter posterior times the nine ppE factors (Eq. 6); the basic-parameter network is not described.
models.inputs: 1 s whitened strain from two LIGO detectors (H1, L1) at 4096 Hz (20-1024 Hz), per-sequence zero-mean unit-variance normalised, plus the other source parameters (masses, spins, DL, sky, inclination, polarisation, tc, phic, and the other ppE parameters held at GR value 0) as conditioning inputs, normalised to [-1,1]. For a real event the conditioning values are not specified.
models.data: 2e7 simulated training samples (96 parallel processes): BBH signals from PyCBC IMRPhenomXPHM with TIGER ppE phase corrections psi_i -> (1+dchi_i) psi_i (Eqs. 2-3), 15 GR parameters with priors as in Ref. [5] (DL 100-6000 Mpc), uniform ppE priors set so the correction stays below the GR leading term; Gaussian coloured noise from aLIGOZeroDetHighPower (stationary, simulated, whitened by the same PSD). One ppE parameter varied at a time, the rest fixed at GR (0). Test: 1000 independent simulated events for coverage/KS; one injection compared with Bilby/Dynesty; GW150914 real data (GWOSC) as a real-data demonstration.
models.training: Each flow trained independently with the negative conditional log-likelihood (Eq. 7), AdamW (lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4), batch size 2048, up to 200 epochs, early stopping after 15 epochs without validation improvement (best snapshot restored), dropout 0.1 on all fully connected layers, gradient clipping and a learning-rate scheduler (type not stated). 8-13 h per parameter on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (PyTorch 2.5.1, CUDA 12.4).
models.results: For 1000 injections the PIT KS p-values are 0.36-0.91 for all nine parameters (all above 0.05) and coverage curves lie within about 0.05 of the diagonal. On one test event the NPE and Dynesty 90% intervals both contain the (unstated) truth, with NPE narrower for dchi0 and dchi2 and wider for dchi1, dchi3 and dchi6; for dchi4-dchi7 both are essentially prior-wide (90% widths ~1.7-1.83 against 1.8 for the prior). Run time: MCMC 2.1e4-4.5e4 s per parameter vs NPE 0.2-0.4 s, a speed-up of about 9e4 (8.8e4 from the table means). On GW150914 the BBH parameters are m1=36.07 (+2.51 -3.68), m2=30.27 (+1.84 -2.93), chi_eff=-0.02, DL=439 (+29 -40) Mpc versus published 35.6, 30.6, -0.01, 440 (+150 -170); ppE posteriors for dchi3-dchi7 are prior-wide with tails; dchi0 and dchi2 (0PN, 1PN) bulk sits away from GR (0), unremarked.
models.code: No code, data or trained-model link in the paper (no code/data availability statement). Searches on GitHub (arXiv id, title keywords, 'factorized NPE ppE', 'ppE neural posterior', 'TIGER normalizing flow') and the web found no repository; GitHub API 2026-10-17 returned 0 results. Built on public PyCBC, Bilby and (conceptually) DINGO.
models.gaps: The injection used for the single-event NPE/MCMC comparison (true ppE value, SNR, masses) is not stated, and the other parameters used for conditioning at test and on GW150914 are not stated; coverage tests with true conditioning parameters are not an end-to-end posterior. The basic-parameter NPE of Eq. 6 is not described, though results for m1, m2, chi_eff, DL are shown. Whether the MCMC varied other parameters or only one ppE parameter is not stated; MCMC hardware not stated. No coverage test on real or non-stationary noise; the authors acknowledge the GW150914 posteriors are affected by training on Gaussian noise. Parameters dchi3-dchi7 are prior-dominated, so calibration passes trivially. No ppE results from LVK TIGER on GW150914 are quantitatively compared. No ablation of the factorisation versus a joint flow.
models.adaptation_notes: Factorised NPE for ppE tests.

suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Their 90% widths are 1.71-1.83 (NPE) against 1.8 for the uniform [-1,1] prior (dchi7 NPE 1.832 exceeds it); Fig 4 violins for 2PN to 3.5PN fill the prior box. The KS/coverage test passes trivially for a posterior equal to the prior, so it does not show information is extracted for these parameters.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Conclusion that the MCMC 'requires over 10 hours' per event and the 9e4 speed-up
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Table II MCMC times are 20943-44818 s (5.8-12.4 h); only two of nine exceed 10 h (36205 s, 44818 s); mean 30046 s = 8.3 h. The 9e4 ratio holds for the mean, but excludes 8-13 h of training per parameter and the unequal hardware (MCMC hardware unstated).

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Explanation that NPE posteriors are narrower than MCMC because MCMC is trapped in a local mode
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: No controlled test supports it: nested sampling with 4096 live points is not a single random-walk chain, no multimodality diagnostic is shown, and the narrower NPE interval in a single event is not evidence of correctness (coverage was tested on separate injections, with conditioning parameters supplied).

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: GW150914 ppE posteriors described as in good agreement with existing results
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Fig 6 shows dchi0 narrowly peaked near +0.2 and dchi2 (1PN) peaked near -0.65 with GR (0) in the tail; dchi1 piled at the upper edge. No quantitative comparison with LVK TIGER bounds is given, and Table III compares only the four BBH parameters. DL is 4.6x narrower than published and the inclination 1.56 (+0.06 -0.04) is a tight edge-on peak, unlike the published GW150914 inclination posterior.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: Violin plots for GW150914 (Fig 6) extend to -5 and +4.3
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: The priors and training support are [-1,1] (normalised); a flow trained on the bounded prior should not place posterior mass at |value|>1, so these tails are either KDE smoothing or out-of-support samples; text does not explain.

suspected_errors_extracted.claim: ppE list 'nine ppE parameters (dchi0 to dchi7)'
suspected_errors_extracted.evidence: Table I and Figs 4-6 show nine entries (dchi0-dchi4, dchi5l, dchi6, dchi6l, dchi7) while the text repeatedly writes dchi0 to dchi7 for eight and sums Eq. 6 over i=7..15; the labelling is inconsistent but the results are unaffected.

models.title: Dragonn: genetic-algorithm search over CNN hyperparameters for CBC detection
models.architecture: Free-form nets assembled by a genetic algorithm (Dragonn): 0-10 hidden layers, each of type dense, conv, pooling or dropout with its own activation (ReLU, ELU, sigmoid, tanh, SELU, GELU, swish, softmax), neurons/filters/kernel/stride 1-128, dilation 0-64, pool 1-32, dropout 0-1; fixed dense output. The best trial ('Model 37', generation 1) is not described layer by layer.
models.inputs: As the Ch. 4 CBC set: whitened 1 s at 2048 Hz, single detector (L1).
models.data: Real O3 L1 noise, cuPhenom IMRPhenomD BBH, masses U(5,95), SNR U(8,15). During part of generation 1, WNB 'glitches' were by mistake injected into 50% of examples, including signal examples and the validation set.
models.training: Each genome trained from scratch with the Ch. 4 settings (Adam 1e-4, batch 32) but patience 1 epoch. GA: 4 generations x 200 genomes = 800 trials; roulette-wheel selection, uniform crossover, 5% per-gene mutation. Fitness: fraction of validation examples above optimal SNR 8 detected at a threshold calibrated to a FAR of 0.01 Hz.
models.results: Average fitness, accuracy and loss improve across generations, but the top three trials (fitness 0.9423, 0.9337, 0.9215) are all generation-1 models trained on the accidentally WNB-contaminated data; the best keeps higher efficiency at SNR ~6 and low FAR than the literature CNNs but plateaus below 100% at high SNR. The owner reads this as a possible 'inoculation' effect, unconfirmed.
models.code: Dragonn is part of GravyFlow (thesis); an earlier C version was used to design the MLy models (skliris2024).
models.gaps: Architecture of the best model; population per generation for the contaminated part (text says first 50); seeds; generation-3 training panel (the figure repeats generation 2).

models.title: Skywarp: attention-based detection of gravitational-wave compact binary coalescences
models.architecture: Transformer-encoder classifiers, three variants. (1) Pure attention: input reshaped to 512 chunks of 16 samples, a kernel-1 conv to 128 features, positional encoding, 8 attention blocks (8 heads, head size 16, dense 128 and 8 with dropout 0.5, residual), dense 64 (dropout 0.5), 2-way softmax. (2) Conv attention: a CNN head (per figure: conv 64 k8, pool 8, conv 32 k8, conv 32 k16, pool 6, conv 16 k16, conv 16 k32, pool 4, conv 128 k1; ReLU) as embedding, positional encoding, the same 8 attention blocks, dense 500 (dropout 0.5), 2-way softmax. (3) Conv attention single: as (2) with one attention block (after Jiang et al.). Hyperparameters by manual trial and error.
models.inputs: Whitened single-detector strain, 1 s on-source (16 s off-source for the whitening layer); sample rate 2048 Hz in the training table (the pure-attention text says 8192 Hz).
models.data: Real O3 LIGO Livingston noise (earlier GravyFlow version, 3600 s acquisition batches); cuPhenom IMRPhenomD BBH, masses U(5,95) Msun, aligned spin U(-0.5,0.5), optimal SNR U(8,20).
models.training: Adam lr 1e-4, batch 32; 1e6 generated examples per epoch, 1e4 validation examples. Baseline is the thesis's Gabbard reproduction trained on the same data.
models.results: Conv-attention hybrids match or slightly beat the Gabbard CNN: equal within noise at 0.1 and 0.01 Hz; at 0.001 Hz the 8-block model leads (63.3% vs 57.6% at SNR 8); at 1e-4 Hz only it and the CNN keep any efficiency (38.4% vs 8.7% at SNR 8) at thresholds above 0.999. Pure attention with chunk embedding is clearly worst. The owner calls the advantage small and possibly training variance.
models.code: GravyFlow pipeline for data and training (thesis); model code and weights not stated as released.
models.gaps: Patience and epoch count; parameter counts; seeds or repeated trainings; validation noise duration behind each FAR; sample rate conflict for the pure-attention model; whether the conv head is exactly Gabbard's.

models.title: Overlapnet: classifying single versus overlapping CBC signals
models.architecture: The Gabbard et al. 1D CNN (as drawn in Ch. 4) applied to two-detector input, softmax binary output (score 1 = two signals). A regression variant (linear output) for the two merger times failed because of a labelling error.
models.inputs: Unwhitened H1 and L1 strain, 16 s at 1024 Hz, every example containing at least one BBH signal.
models.data: Static set by P. J. Relton: aLIGO design-PSD Gaussian noise for H1 and L1, unwhitened; LALSimulation IMRPhenomTPHM BBH, primary mass 10-70 Msun, mass ratio 0.1-1; luminosity-distance scaling (power law base 2 x 145 + 5 Mpc) giving network SNR 5-100; 16 s at 1024 Hz; pairs have merger separations <= 2 s. Training: 2e5 singles and 2e5 pairs from a bank of 2e5 waveforms (1e5 pairs, each in two noise realisations); validation 2e4 + 2e4 with new seeds.
models.training: Adam lr 1e-4, batch 32, scale factor 1e21; threshold 0.5 (classes treated as equally costly, so no FAR calibration).
models.results: Most pairs are recognised when both signals have network SNR above ~10 and almost all singles are recognised; performance falls for merger separations below 0.8 s and sharply below 0.2 s. Chirp mass and mass ratio have little effect. The owner suspects the model partly uses total excess power.
models.code: Thesis code; not stated as released.
models.gaps: No overall accuracy or confusion matrix; no matched-filter comparison in the chapter despite the claim of parity; number of epochs and stopping rule.

models.title: CrossWave: cross-detector attention for the parameter estimation of overlapping CBC signals
models.architecture: Two-branch network for H1 and L1: per-detector denoising autoencoder heads (encoder from the Gabbard CNN, mirrored decoder with transpose convolutions and upsampling; independent weights, trained jointly, not pre-trained), a weight-shared Gabbard-style feature extractor and kernel-1 conv embedding (128), positional encoding, three blocks each with self-attention per branch and cross-attention in both directions (8 heads, head size 16, dense 128 and 8, dropout 0.5), concatenation, dense 500 (dropout 0.5) and the regression output. A smaller variant (three self-attention blocks then one cross-attention) was trialled and dropped.
models.inputs: Unwhitened H1 and L1 strain, 16 s at 1024 Hz; pairs of overlapping BBH signals only.
models.data: Static set by P. J. Relton: aLIGO design-PSD Gaussian noise for H1 and L1, unwhitened; LALSimulation IMRPhenomTPHM BBH, primary mass 10-70 Msun, mass ratio 0.1-1; luminosity-distance scaling (power law base 2 x 145 + 5 Mpc) giving network SNR 5-100; 16 s at 1024 Hz; pairs have merger separations <= 2 s. Singles removed: 2e5 training pairs, 2e4 validation pairs.
models.training: Adam lr 1e-4, batch 32; 24 regression targets per example (merger times at H1, L1 and geocentre, both masses, luminosity distance and six spin components for each of signals A and B), labels normalised to [0,1]; ReLU output.
models.results: Merger times recovered with R^2 0.963-0.968 and mean absolute errors of 0.09-0.10 s (errors rise sharply when the two mergers nearly coincide, including A and B swaps along the error = separation line); component masses partly (R^2 0.61-0.72); spin z weakly; spin x, y and luminosity distance not at all (negative R^2 for distance). Point estimates only, no uncertainty.
models.code: Thesis code; not stated as released.
models.gaps: Loss function; epochs; parameter count; no comparison with a sampler or other PE method; no calibration; small-model results not shown; the signal-B normalisation error left in.

Relton: aLIGO design-PSD Gaussian noise for H1 and L1, unwhitened; LALSimulation IMRPhenomTPHM BBH, primary mass 10-70 Msun, mass ratio 0.1-1; luminosity-distance scaling (power law base 2 x 145 + 5 Mpc) giving network SNR 5-100; 16 s at 1024 Hz; pairs have merger separations <= 2 s

models.runtime_unread: No paper in the archive for the runtime pass; the entry was catalogued from elsewhere (Owner's own thesis: Typst chapter sources and figure PNGs read directly; compiled PDF not rendered.)

axes.value: Point estimates: merger-time MAE 0.09-0.10 s (R^2 ~0.96); mass MAE 5.5-8.0 Msun; no calibration or sampler comparison

comparability.what_differs: Regression on a private Gaussian design-PSD set of pairs; no posterior, no P-P test, no baseline.
highlighted_errors: Validation size is 2e5 pairs in the results text but 2e4 in the dataset section.
Some signal-B merger-time labels were normalised below zero and cannot be reached by the ReLU output; those examples are dropped from the plots.

models.comparability_notes_extractor: Owner's own work; P. J. Relton's datasets reused without further input from him. The owner calls the non-time parameters a demonstration of what does not work.
suspected_errors_extracted: Results text says 2e5 pair validation examples; the dataset section gives 2e4.
Label section says the luminosity distance lies between 500 and 700 Mpc, while the generation rule has a 5 Mpc minimum and the distance MAE is 23 Mpc.
Normalisation passage says some signal-B labels were 'less than one'; the caption and conclusion say less than zero.
Figure caption calls ReLU the 'loss function'; it is the output activation.
CrossWave diagram ends in a two-neuron softmax labelled 'Binary Classification' although the model regresses 24 parameters.
Conclusion puts the labelling error on the small network's PE trial; the chapter puts it on the Overlapnet regression attempt.
